articles.title_original: Toward Energy‐Efficient Metal Oxide Semiconductor‐Based Sensor Technologies
articles.title_en: Review outlines energy-efficient metal oxide semiconductor sensors
articles.excerpt_original: ABSTRACT As the first interface between electronic systems and the external environment, sensors play an essential role in converting real‐world stimuli into electrical information. With the expansion of sensor applications toward portable, wearable, Internet of things (IoT), and AI‐integrated platforms, energy consumption has become a critical factor governing their practical usability. Among various semiconductor‐based sensing materials, metal oxide semiconductor (MOS) materials are particularly promising for energy‐efficient sensors because their wide bandgaps provide an inherent advantage in suppressing standby current in MOS‐based sensor devices. However, practical MOS‐based sensors cannot be optimized by reducing standby current alone, because additional energy consumption can arise from modality‐specific sensing processes during operation. Therefore, this review analyzes energy‐consumption mechanisms in MOS‐based sensors and discusses device‐level strategies for reducing modality‐dependent energy requirements. Beyond individual sensor devices, this review further addresses system‐level energy issues associated with signal transfer and processing, highlighting near‐sensor and in‐sensor computing architectures. Overall, this work emphasizes that energy‐efficient MOS‐based sensor technologies require an integrated design framework that considers material properties, sensing mechanisms, device operation, and system architecture together.
articles.summary_en: A review examines how metal oxide semiconductor sensors can reduce energy consumption through low standby currents, optimized sensing mechanisms, and near-sensor or in-sensor computing. articles.title_original: Undercooled Liquid Metallic Core–Shell Particles Enabling Heatless Metal–Semiconductor Bonding for Micro-Transfer Printed GaN

articles.excerpt_original: Abstract Heterogeneous integration of Gallium Nitride (GaN) high-electron-mobility transistors (HEMTs) via micro-transfer printing (μTP) offers a scalable route to address critical thermal management and integration challenges for high-power and high-frequency applications. However, traditional polymer adhesives used in the printing process create a thermal bottleneck due to their low thermal conductivity. This work introduces a room-temperature, heatless soldering mechanism at the device level utilizing undercooled liquid metallic core–shell (ULMCS) particles. Synthesized via the shearing liquids into complex particles (SLICE) method, these Field’s metal (Bi/In/Sn) particles are encapsulated in a self-limiting 10 nm oxide shell, maintaining a metastable liquid state until mechanical rupture triggers spontaneous solidification. To test this, GaN/AlGaN coupons were released from Qromis Substrate Technology wafers and printed onto silicon substrates using ULCMS particles. Printing parameters, including shear speed and shear distance, were optimized to ensure consistent adhesion. While initial μTP using compliant polydimethylsiloxane (PDMS) stamps achieved high transfer yields, cross-sectional analysis revealed incomplete coalescence due to insufficient pressure applied by the stamp. To resolve this, a dual-stage integration framework was developed, incorporating a secondary rigid glass stamping step. This process successfully created a dense, metallic adhesion layer, providing a robust and cost-effective pathway for the integration of GaN devices for thermal management applications.
articles.summary_en: Researchers demonstrated room-temperature, heatless bonding of GaN/AlGaN devices onto silicon using oxide-encapsulated Field’s metal particles. articles.title_original: Spontaneous Propagation of Molecular Precursor Films on Graphene: Driving and Resistive Mechanisms
articles.title_en: Molecular Precursor Films Spread Diffusively on Graphene
articles.excerpt_original: Molecular precursor films play an important role in total wetting, yet their propagation dynamics are difficult to isolate in finite nanodroplet systems because continuous droplet deformation and depletion alter the capillary driving conditions. Molecular dynamics simulations are employed to investigate the spreading of γ-valerolactone (GVL) and N,N-dimethylformamide (DMF) on pristine graphene. Both nanodroplets exhibit total wetting and spontaneously form molecularly thin precursor films. To separate precursor-film propagation from bulk-droplet evolution, a reservoir-based configuration is constructed in which liquid is supplied through a nanoscale gap. Following an initial entrance transient, a quasi-static meniscus forms and maintains approximately constant driving conditions. The precursor film subsequently propagates according to diffusive scaling, (L2 ~ t), while its directly calculated velocity varies inversely with the propagation length, (Vx ~ L-1). GVL exhibits slower propagation and a more gradual decrease in total internal energy than DMF. Thermodynamic integration shows that GVL has a lower spreading coefficient and weaker adhesion to graphene. The thickness-dependent internal film pressure also produces a smaller pressure difference between the meniscus and the ultrathin film for GVL. In addition, its lower two-dimensional self-diffusion coefficient indicates reduced interfacial molecular mobility and greater spreading resistance. These results demonstrate that precursor-film propagation is governed by the combined effects of the thermodynamic driving force, thickness-dependent film pressure, and interfacial molecular transport.

articles.excerpt_original: Abstract Selective elimination of CO2 from H2-containing streams requires surface sites that preferentially stabilize CO2 while limiting the H2 uptake. This work explores a structure-oriented modification strategy for monolayer graphene by introducing phosphorus-centered groups with different phenyl/hydroxyl environments at a fixed nominal grafting site density. GCMC simulations were used to quantify pure-gas and binary CO2/H2 adsorption, while DFT-derived electrostatic potential, van der Waals potential, and charge-density distributions were analyzed to connect surface polarity with adsorption behavior. The results show that phosphoryl functionality strengthens the CO2 affinity, while phenyl substitution modifies the spatial distribution of favorable adsorption regions without promoting H2 adsorption. Noncovalent interaction and adsorption energy analyses further indicate a stronger local binding preference of G-DPPA toward CO2 than H2, consistent with the preferential CO2 adsorption observed in the GCMC simulations. Among the investigated models, diphenylphosphinic acid-functionalized graphene (G-DPPA) exhibits the most favorable separation behavior. At 273 K and 1 bar, its CO2 uptake is 44.5% higher than that of pristine graphene, and the CO2/H2 selectivity for an equimolar mixture increases by 70.66%, giving an adsorbed-phase CO2 fraction of ∼96%.
articles.summary_en: Simulations show that diphenylphosphinic acid-functionalized graphene increases CO2 uptake by 44.5% versus pristine graphene and raises equimolar CO2/H2 selectivity by 70.66%. articles.excerpt_original: The strategic integration of the tunable band gap and high carrier mobility of MoS2 with the exceptional electrical conductivity of graphene offers a compelling route to circumvent the intrinsic sensing limitations of each material in isolation. Within the resulting van der Waals heterostructures, synergistic interlayer electronic coupling substantially reshapes the optoelectronic response. In particular, the MoS2/graphene interface exhibits an ultraviolet absorption coefficient of approximately 3.5 × 105 cm−1 at 350 nm, an enhancement of about 20% relative to pristine MoS2. First-principles density functional theory (DFT) calculations further show that tuning the interlayer spacing induces a finite band gap in graphene, attaining 67.8 meV at a compressed separation of 2.3 Å. Building on these electronic insights, the gas-sensing performance of the MoS2/graphene heterostructure was evaluated toward CO, CO2, NO, and HF gases. The adsorption energies, supported by electronegativity analysis, were consistently negative for oxidizing (CO2, NO), reducing (CO), and corrosive (HF) molecules, namely −70 meV, −51 meV, −363 meV, and −127 meV for CO, CO2, NO, and HF, respectively, a trend corroborated by electronegativity analysis. This energetically favorable adsorption underscores the strong gas–surface interactions enabled by the heterointerface, revealing a superior sensing response compared to either MoS2 or graphene alone. These results highlight the promising potential of MoS2/graphene heterostructures for next-generation, high-sensitivity gas-monitoring technologies.

articles.excerpt_original: Abstract MXene/polymer composites have attracted sustained attention for electromagnetic interference (EMI) shielding, for which effective conductive-network construction is central to performance. However, the role of conductive networks in regulating EMI shielding from the dual perspectives of microscale interfaces and macroscale structures remains incompletely understood. To address this issue, this review systematically summarizes advances and remaining challenges across three key dimensions: the intrinsic conductivity of MXene nanosheets, interfacial modulation strategies, and macrostructural design principles. Representative approaches for improving EMI shielding performance through engineered conductive-network architectures are then critically discussed. Finally, current challenges, targeted recommendations, and future directions for controlling the EMI shielding performance of MXene/polymer composites through conductive-network engineering are outlined.
articles.summary_en: A review examines how MXene conductivity, interfacial engineering, and macrostructural design affect electromagnetic-interference shielding in MXene/polymer composites. It identifies remaining challenges and research directions for controlling shielding performance through conductive-network architecture.

articles.title_original: Covalently Integrated MXene–Fluorinated Polymer Electrolytes for 714 Wh Kg −1 Lithium–Metal Batteries
articles.title_en: Covalent MXene–Polymer Electrolyte Enables High-Energy Lithium–Metal Batteries
articles.excerpt_original: ABSTRACT Polymer electrolytes are promising for high‐energy and safe lithium–metal batteries yet limited by inadequate mechanical integrity, sluggish Li + transport, and unstable electrode–electrolyte interfaces. Here, we report a covalently integrated MXene–fluorinated gel polymer electrolyte (MF‐GPE) through in situ polymerization. Acrylate‐grafted MXene nanosheets act as chemically anchored crosslinkers within a fluorinated polymer network, distinguishing from conventional physically blended composites. The covalent framework not only mechanically reinforces the polymer matrix but also regulates Li + solvation structure and lowers the activation energy for Li + transport. Consequently, the MF‐GPE enables uniform lithium deposition and constructs robust, inorganic‐rich interphases on both lithium–metal anodes and high‐voltage cathodes. It delivers an ionic conductivity of 3.3 mS cm −1 at 25°C and supports stable cycling of LiNi 0.8 Co 0.1 Mn 0.1 O 2 , LiCoO 2 and LiNi 0.5 Mn 1.5 O 4 cathodes at cut‐off voltages up to 4.9 V. Notably, a MF‐GPE based Li||LiCoO 2 pouch cell achieves cell‐level energy densities of 713.9 Wh kg −1 at 4.8 V and 605.2 Wh kg −1 at 4.6 V, maintaining stable operation over 60 cycles, while 18650 cylindrical cells operate stably for 500 cycles. Ah‐class pouch cells demonstrate outstanding safety under nail‐penetration and overcharge tests. These findings establish covalent MXene‐polymer integration to couple ion solvation structure and interphase stabilization for high‐energy, abuse‐tolerant lithium–metal batteries.
articles.summary_en: Researchers developed a covalently integrated MXene–fluorinated gel polymer electrolyte that improves mechanical strength, lithium-ion transport, and electrode-interface stability. Lithium–metal cells reportedly reached 713.9 Wh/kg at the cell level and demonstrated extended cycling and abuse tolerance in pouch and cylindrical formats.

articles.title_original: Fabrication of Pt-decorated MXene–chitosan nanocomposite electrodes for non-enzymatic electrochemical detection of biomolecules
articles.title_en: Pt–MXene–Chitosan Electrodes Enable Non-Enzymatic Biomolecule Detection
articles.excerpt_original: . The estimated LOD and LOQ are 0.30 µM and 1.01 µM, respectively. The fabricated Pt/MX-Chit-ITO electrode offers a cost-effective and fast detection platform for biosensing applications.
articles.summary_en: Researchers fabricated platinum-decorated MXene–chitosan nanocomposite electrodes for electrochemical biosensing. The Pt/MX-Chit-ITO platform achieved estimated detection and quantification limits of 0.30 µM and 1.01 µM, respectively.

articles.title_original: Nanoparticle Modification of Acrylic-Based Soft Denture Liner: Effects of Samarium Oxide, Boron Nitride and Titanium Dioxide on Surface, Chemical and Adhesive Properties
articles.title_en: Nanoparticles Improve Acrylic Denture Liner Properties in vitro
articles.excerpt_original: Abstract Background This in vitro study evaluated the effects of incorporating samarium oxide (Sm₂O₃), boron nitride (BN), and titanium dioxide (TiO₂) nanoparticles into an acrylic-based soft denture liner on residual monomer release, surface roughness, contact angle, and peel bond strength. Methods Ten groups were prepared: a control and groups containing each nanoparticle at 1, 2, and 5 wt%. Surface roughness (Ra) and contact angle were measured by confocal profilometry and optical tensiometry (n = 10), and residual monomer release was determined by HPLC at 12, 24, and 72 hours (n = 10). Peel bond strength was assessed by 180° peel testing according to ASTM D903-98 (n = 8). Data were analyzed by one-way ANOVA with Tukey HSD test, and by two-way ANOVA for monomer release ( P <.05). Results All nanoparticle groups released significantly less residual monomer than the control at all time points ( P <.05). Surface roughness decreased significantly only in the Sm₂O₃-containing S1 and S2 groups. Contact angle was significantly higher than that of the control in most TiO₂ and Sm₂O₃ groups. All groups exceeded the clinically acceptable peel bond strength threshold; the highest value (S5, 1.461 ± 0.598 N/mm) did not differ significantly from that of the control. Conclusion The effects of nanoparticle incorporation depended on particle type and concentration. Sm₂O₃ showed a favorable overall profile, reducing residual monomer release and, at low and medium concentrations, surface roughness, while maintaining bond strength above the clinical threshold, and is a promising additive candidate for acrylic-based soft denture liners. Further research is needed.
articles.summary_en: Researchers evaluated samarium oxide, boron nitride and titanium dioxide nanoparticles in acrylic-based soft denture liners. Samarium oxide showed the most favorable overall profile, reducing residual monomer release and surface roughness while maintaining clinically acceptable bond strength.

articles.title_original: Direct Visualization of Polarity‐Driven Carrier Redistribution in Two‐Dimensional In/CdS
articles.title_en: 2D In/CdS Flakes Reveal Polarity-Driven Carrier Separation
articles.excerpt_original: ABSTRACT The intrinsic polarization field (IPF) in wurtzite semiconductors has long been proposed as a means to regulate carrier migration in photocatalytic and optoelectronic systems. However, direct experimental visualization of polarity‐driven charge separation remains challenging because intrinsic polarization effects are often obscured by competing surface fields and structural heterogeneity, leading to long‐standing contradictions between theory and experiment. Here, we fabricate well‐defined two‐dimensional In‐doped CdS single‐crystalline flakes (In/CdS) with exposed polar basal planes, providing a model platform to directly probe polarity‐driven carrier redistribution. Kelvin probe force microscopy, combined with photo‐deposition and single‐molecule fluorescence imaging, reveals opposite carrier accumulation on the two basal surfaces of individual flakes, with the upper surface serving as an electron‐rich reduction site and the bottom surface acting as a hole‐rich oxidation site. The spatially separated carrier distribution enables selective co‐catalyst loading on electron‐accumulated surfaces and boosts photocatalytic H 2 evolution. Ultrafast spectroscopy reveals a long lifetime (>2 µs) of photogenerated electrons and ultrafast electron transfer to co‐catalysts with an efficiency approaching unity. This work provides long‐sought experimental proof of charge separation in polar semiconductors and establishes a paradigm for exploiting intrinsic bulk properties through 2D geometry.
articles.summary_en: Researchers directly visualized opposite electron and hole accumulation on the polar surfaces of two-dimensional indium-doped CdS flakes. The separated carriers enabled selective cocatalyst loading and improved photocatalytic hydrogen evolution, with photogenerated electrons lasting over 2 microseconds.

articles.title_original: Dark Exciton Signatures in the Infrared Transient Absorption of MoS2 Monolayer
articles.title_en: GW+BSE analysis reveals dark-exciton signatures in monolayer MoS2
articles.excerpt_original: Abstract Dark excitons play a central role in the nonequilibrium dynamics of two-dimensional semiconductors but remain difficult to characterize. Interexciton transient absorption (exc-tr-abs) in experiments, with probes tuned in the exciton–exciton transitions energy range, can detect excitations from any populated dark excitons, including symmetry-forbidden, spin-forbidden, and finite-momentum ones. In this work, we develop a GW+BSE scheme for computing exc-tr-abs spectra from arbitrary populated exciton distributions. These dark excitons are included equally by evaluating exciton–exciton dipoles in a locally smooth gauge, including intra- and interband contributions. For monolayer MoS2, the exc-tr-abs signal arises from the Γ, K, M, and Q valleys, differing substantially from the Γ-only interpretation. Exciton–exciton dipoles show similar intensities across these valleys, while their weights are dictated by initial excitonic populations. State- and spin-resolved analyses assign the peaks to 1s → 2p and 1s → 3p transitions from both spin-flip and spin-conserving A and B excitons across valleys and momenta.
articles.summary_en: Researchers developed a computational method to calculate interexciton transient-absorption spectra for arbitrary dark-exciton populations. Applied to monolayer MoS2, the analysis identifies contributions from multiple valleys and assigns peaks to excitonic transitions involving spin-flip and spin-conserving states.

articles.title_original: Dynamic Metal–Semiconductor Electrical Interfaces in Model Cu|ZnO Hydrogenation Catalyst Structures
articles.title_en: Hydrogen Dynamically Alters Cu–ZnO Catalyst Interfaces
articles.excerpt_original: Abstract Cu/ZnO/Al2O3 catalysts are commonly used for methanol synthesis; yet, the chemical state of the Cu|ZnO interface remains debated. Recent studies have suggested that interfacial fields and junction effects could explain observed shifts in binding energies of intermediates (e.g., CO2δ− and HCOO−) involved in the reduction of CO2 to methanol on Cu|ZnO. In this study, we probe Cu|ZnO interfacial chemistry by measuring junction electrical characteristics under N2, CO2, and H2 gas mixtures from 50 to 250 °C and up to 10 bar. The pristine interface behaves as a nonideal rectifying Schottky diode, and H2 exposure increases n-type donor density in the ZnO and lowers Schottky-barrier height, with full transition to an ohmic junction. These observations imply the electrostatic potential gradient at the putative active-catalyst interface could change under reaction conditions, depending on the precise composition of the oxide phase. H-doping of ZnO is reversed in a N2 or CO2 stream at 200 °C without any O2, inconsistent with proposed Cu–Zn alloying or oxygen-vacancy formation mechanisms suggested in studies of methanol synthesis on Cu/ZnO/Al2O3 catalysts, and instead suggests reversible hydrogen doping of ZnO. The addition of CO2 reduces the rate of H doping into ZnO, while water addition strongly suppresses it. The time scale for the H-doping of Cu|ZnO devices by H2 is much longer than that estimated for H diffusion in bulk ZnO, suggesting that H2 dissociation and/or H insertion into ZnO are the elementary steps governing the rate of H doping of the ZnO. Junction electrical measurements can thus inform how electro-active interfaces invoked in catalysis evolve under reaction conditions.
articles.summary_en: Measurements show that hydrogen converts model Cu|ZnO interfaces from rectifying Schottky diodes to ohmic junctions by reversibly increasing ZnO donor density and lowering the Schottky barrier. The findings indicate that electrostatic catalyst interfaces evolve under reaction conditions and challenge proposed Cu–Zn alloying or oxygen-vacancy explanations for the observed behavior.

articles.title_original: Cellulose Nanopaper‐Regulated Flexible Organic Semiconductor Heterointerface for Ultrasensitive and Wireless Detection of a Nerve Agent Simulant
articles.title_en: Cellulose nanopaper sensor enables wireless detection of nerve-agent simulant
articles.excerpt_original: ABSTRACT Flexible chemiresistive sensors are promising for portable warning, environmental monitoring, and personal protection against hazardous volatile chemicals. Herein, a flexible organic semiconductor sensor based on wood‐derived cellulose nanopaper (WCN) and poly(9,9‐dioctylfluorene‐alt‐benzothiadiazole) (F8BT) is developed for the ultrasensitive detection of diethyl chlorophosphate (DCP), a representative nerve agent simulant. WCN acts as a lightweight and flexible substrate with a stable interfacial environment, while F8BT serves as the active sensing layer for molecular recognition and charge transduction. The resulting F8BT‐WCN heterointerface significantly enhances DCP sensing performance, delivering a response of 74% to 132 ppm DCP, a response time of 2 s, a detection limit of 0.65 ppb, and good concentration dependence over 1.68 ppb–132 ppm. The sensor also exhibits excellent selectivity and stable responses under mechanical deformation, humidity variation, and long‐term storage. In addition, a passive wireless device was developed to enable contactless readout of DCP‐induced sensing signals, demonstrating the feasibility of wireless integration. This work provides an effective strategy for developing flexible and high‐performance gas sensors for portable hazardous vapor detection.
articles.summary_en: Researchers developed a flexible organic semiconductor sensor using wood-derived cellulose nanopaper and F8BT to detect diethyl chlorophosphate, a nerve-agent simulant, with a reported 0.65 ppb detection limit and 2-second response. A passive wireless readout demonstrated potential for portable hazardous-vapor monitoring and personal protection.

articles.title_original: Fabrication of Waterborne Polyurethane Flexible Strain Sensors Based on KH560-MXene/MWCNTs Synergistic Effects and the Application in Motion Posture Monitoring
articles.title_en: Waterborne polyurethane MXene/MWCNT strain sensor enables motion monitoring
articles.excerpt_original: Abstract Flexible sensors serve as the core component of wearable electronics and intelligent health monitoring devices, possessing enormous application potential in the fields of human physiological signal acquisition and motion behavior detection. Nevertheless, flexible sensing materials generally suffer from poor environmental stability, weak anti-interference capability of sensing signals, and inevitable degradation of sensing performance during long-term cyclic operation, which severely restrict their large-scale practical applications. To address these issues, waterborne polyurethane (WPU) is adopted as the flexible matrix, modified MXene nanosheets with KH560 and multi-walled carbon nanotubes (MWCNTs) were introduced as hybrid conductive fillers. An integrated high-performance flexible strain sensor is fabricated via a solution blending and casting strategy. Through hydrogen bonding and electrostatic adsorption effects, a 1D-2D interconnected conductive network is constructed, where MXene acts as the primary conductive unit and MWCNTs function as interconnection bridging segments. This flexible sensor based on the composite system exhibits superior comprehensive performances, including a high gauge factor of 2.81, a broad strain detection range of 0-2800%, rapid response and recovery times of 150 ms and 120 ms, as well as excellent cycling stability over 3000 cycles. Density functional theory (DFT) calculations elucidate the interfacial mechanism of the MXene/MWCNTs heterojunction, verifying that the sensing mechanism originates from the synergistic effect of band structure evolution and conductive network reconstruction. Furthermore, the sensor enables real-time monitoring of electromyographic signals during human movements, demonstrating great application poten
articles.summary_en: Researchers developed a flexible strain sensor using KH560-modified MXene and multi-walled carbon nanotubes in a waterborne polyurethane matrix. The device combines a 0–2800% strain range, 2.81 gauge factor, rapid response, and stability over 3,000 cycles, enabling real-time electromyographic motion monitoring.

articles.title_original: In Situ Growth of δ-MnO2 Nanosheets on K+ Intercalation Nb2CT x MXene for Aqueous Zinc-Ion Battery Cathodes
articles.title_en: K+-Intercalated Nb2CTx MXene–MnO2 Cathode Improves Aqueous Zinc-Ion Batteries
articles.excerpt_original: Abstract Aqueous zinc-ion batteries (AZIBs) are regarded as a feasible option for large-scale energy storage, benefiting from intrinsic safety, resource availability, and cost-effectiveness. Nevertheless, their advancement is hindered by the sluggish ion-transport kinetics and poor structural stability of cathode materials during cycling. In this work, K+-intercalation Nb2CTx MXene was coupled with δ-MnO2 nanosheets via a mild water bath in situ growth strategy to prepare K-Nb2C@MnO2 heterojunction composite cathodes. Electrochemical evaluations revealed that the as-obtained composite delivers a high specific capacity of 367.51 mAh g−1 at 0.1 A g−1. Even under 3.0 A g−1, decent capacity retention can be obtained over 1000 continuous cycles, with the Coulombic efficiency stably kept above 96%. Electrochemical impedance spectroscopy measurements verified the dramatically decreased charge-transfer resistance and improved Zn2+ diffusion capability. Such improvements originate largely from the constructed heterointerfaces, which effectively modulate the overall electrochemical reaction kinetics. This work offers an effective pathway for engineering interlayer structures and enhancing interfacial activity, providing guidance for the design of niobium-based MXene composite cathodes in high-performance AZIBs.
articles.summary_en: Researchers grew δ-MnO2 nanosheets in situ on K+-intercalated Nb2CTx MXene to create a heterojunction cathode for aqueous zinc-ion batteries. The composite delivered 367.51 mAh g−1 at 0.1 A g−1 and retained performance over 1,000 cycles at 3.0 A g−1, attributed to improved charge transfer and Zn2+ diffusion.

articles.title_en: 3D Boron Nitride–Epoxy Composites Improve Thermal and Tribological Performance

articles.title_original: A Generic and High‐Throughput Capillary‐Driven Shear Assembly for Fabrication of Highly Aligned Nanomaterials
articles.title_en: Capillary-driven shear assembly enables aligned, high-conductivity graphene architectures
articles.excerpt_original: ABSTRACT Assembling two‐dimensional (2D) nanomaterials into macroscopic architectures that retain their exceptional intrinsic properties is pivotal for next‐generation functional devices. However, a persistent trade‐off remains between structural precision and fabrication throughput: scalable techniques often succumb to Brownian‐induced orientation relaxation, yielding loosely packed, isotropic networks, while precision‐oriented methods lack industrial scalability. Herein, we demonstrate a capillary‐driven shear assembly (CDSA) strategy—a continuous, hydrodynamically driven approach that leverages the synergy of capillary pressure and fluid dynamics to fabricate highly aligned, densified nanocomposites. Unlike conventional strategies, the CDSA strategy utilizes capillary forces generated by porous media to create a confined horizontal shear flow, which aligns the nanosheets horizontally at the interface. This strategy not only boosts assembly speed, but also proves universally applicable to a diverse library of 2D materials, including graphene oxide (GO), MXene, MoS 2 , and h‐BN. Importantly, after graphitization treatments, g‐CDSA‐GO exhibits a high in‐plane thermal conductivity. Further incorporation of polyimide‐derived graphitic bridges increases the through‐plane thermal conductivity to 21.3 W m −1 K −1 while maintaining an in‐plane value of 1406 W m −1 K −1 . These results establish CDSA as a scalable route for constructing highly ordered 2D architectures.
articles.summary_en: Researchers demonstrate a continuous capillary-driven shear assembly method for rapidly aligning and densifying graphene oxide and other two-dimensional nanomaterials. After graphitization and incorporation of graphitic bridges, the graphene-based architecture achieves 1,406 W m⁻¹ K⁻¹ in-plane and 21.3 W m⁻¹ K⁻¹ through-plane thermal conductivity, indicating potential for scalable thermal-management materials.

articles.title_original: Spin‐Selective Transport in Chiral 2D Transition Metal Dichalcogenide Superlattices: Mechanisms and Device Applications
articles.title_en: Review Maps Spin-Selective Transport in Chiral TMD Superlattices
articles.excerpt_original: The chiral-induced spin selectivity (CISS) effect, enabling efficient spin polarization without external magnetic fields, has positioned chiral two-dimensional (2D) materials as promising platforms for next-generation spintronics, quantum technologies, and spin-dependent catalysis. Among these, 2D transition metal dichalcogenide (TMD) superlattices offer a uniquely tunable platform, where molecular chirality incorporated into inorganic frameworks enables precise control over spin polarization through tailored chiral-host interactions. Despite significant progress, a critical gap remains in understanding how chirality transfers from intercalated molecules to TMD host lattices and bridges fundamental CISS mechanisms with device-ready performance. This review addresses this gap by providing a comprehensive and critical assessment of chiral TMD superlattices formed through molecular intercalation. We discuss proposed CISS mechanisms, including spin-orbit coupling and spinterface effects, and critically evaluate experimental and theoretical characterization techniques. We then present advances in synthetic strategies that enable precise control over chiral architectures, offering insights pivotal for designing high-performance spin-based devices. Building on these foundations, we explore emerging applications in spin optoelectronics, spin electrocatalysis, and chiral sensing, while offering critical analysis of the underlying mechanisms driving their enhanced performance. Finally, we identify key challenges and propose a roadmap for future research and innovation in this dynamic field.
articles.summary_en: A review examines how molecular chirality transfers into two-dimensional transition metal dichalcogenide superlattices to enable spin polarization without external magnetic fields. It assesses mechanisms, synthesis and characterization strategies, and potential applications in spintronics, spin optoelectronics, spin electrocatalysis and chiral sensing.

articles.title_original: Correlating Defects and Surface Contaminants: Toward Clean Graphene with Improved Mechanical Performance
articles.title_en: Defects and Contamination Reduce CVD Graphene Strength
articles.excerpt_original: Abstract The mechanical performance of large-area chemical vapor deposition (CVD) graphene membranes is often compromised by coexisting lattice defects and surface contamination. However, the underlying synergistic mechanisms remain elusive, particularly regarding how defects mediate contaminant nucleation and how their coupling degrades the mechanical properties of graphene. Here, combining in situ spherical aberration-corrected transmission electron microscopy with controlled contaminant removal and redeposition experiments, we provide atomic-scale experimental validation for the causal correlation between graphene point defects and amorphous carbon contamination on CVD-grown graphene. We further achieve real-time, site-resolved visualization of active carbon species migration and defect-trapping dynamics. Multiscale simulations uncover a defect-mediated kinetic-trapping mechanism: active carbon species migrate rapidly over intact graphene yet become captured and immobilized at defects, with the calculated diffusion coefficient dropping from ∼14.4 to 1.65 nm2 ns–1. Moreover, nanoindentation tests confirm that clean graphene exhibits superior mechanical properties (stiffness: ∼305 N m–1 and fracture force: ∼1900 nN) compared to the contaminated counterpart (stiffness: ∼224 N m–1 and fracture force: ∼1077 nN). Continuum finite-element analysis indicates that the reduced stiffness of unclean graphene cannot be explained by surface contamination alone, supporting the presence of defect-induced softening beneath the contamination. Atomically resolved simulations further reveal that the mechanical response is jointly governed by defect type, contamination, and interfacial bonding. articles.summary_en: Researchers linked point defects to amorphous carbon trapping on CVD graphene, validating a defect-mediated contamination mechanism through microscopy and simulations. Clean graphene showed substantially higher stiffness and fracture force than contaminated material, indicating that defect-induced softening contributes beyond surface contamination alone.

articles.title_original: High‐Performance 2D MXene‐Derived TiO 2 Integrated Optical Polarizers
articles.title_en: MXene-Derived TiO₂ Films Enable High-Performance Optical Polarizers
articles.excerpt_original: ABSTRACT Polarization control is essential for modern optical systems. Recently, 2D materials featuring highly anisotropic absorption across broad wavelength regions have emerged as a promising solution for realizing optical polarizers with operation bandwidths far exceeding those achievable using bulk materials. Despite this, existing 2D‐material‐based optical polarizers face critical limitations in simultaneously delivering high polarizer figures of merit (FOMs), robust power endurance, and scalable fabrication, hindering their practical deployment beyond the laboratory. Here, we overcome this bottleneck by demonstrating optical polarizers through integrating 2D MXene films onto silicon photonic devices and subsequently converting them in situ into 2D titanium dioxide (TiO 2 ). The 2D TiO 2 exhibits significantly improved anisotropic absorption and thermal/chemical stability compared with MXene, enabling the hybrid polarizers that achieve high polarizer FOMs of up to ∼19.3 (a record among 2D‐material‐coated devices) and excellent power tolerance (stable under > 2 W coupled average power), together with a broad operation bandwidth (> 140 nm) and a high fabrication yield (∼98%). We also demonstrate microring resonator polarizers achieving high polarization extinction ratios of up to ∼12 dB. With outstanding overall performance and strong potential for large‐scale manufacturing, these devices represent a solid step toward industrial implementation of 2D‐material‐based optical polarizers.
articles.summary_en: Researchers converted 2D MXene films into TiO₂ on silicon photonic devices, improving anisotropic absorption, thermal and chemical stability, and power tolerance. The polarizers achieved a reported figure of merit of approximately 19.3, bandwidth above 140 nm, and fabrication yield near 98%, indicating potential for scalable photonic manufacturing.

articles.title_original: Polarisation effects on strained B-centres in hBN
articles.title_en: Strain Enables Polarisation Control of hBN Single-Photon Emitters
articles.excerpt_original: Solid-state single-photon emitters are essential for the development of quantum technologies. In hexagonal boron nitride, the B-centre presents promising optical properties, yet its precise atomic structure has remained unresolved. Here, we investigate the impact of uniaxial mechanical strain on the emission polarisation of the B-centre through a combination of confocal microscopy and ab initio structural simulations. We demonstrate that applied uniaxial strain induces discrete rotations of the transition dipole moments, forcing the emitters to realign towards the applied strain axis. This discrete polarisation switching is consistent with the lifting of electronic degeneracy via a strain-induced Jahn–Teller effect. Complementary density-functional theory corroborates this mechanism and identify the neutral C N -C i split-interstitial carbon dimer as a plausible origin of the B-centre. Our findings offer a critical pathway for the deterministic alignment of single-photon emitters to nanophotonic cavities in on-chip architectures.
articles.summary_en: Researchers show that uniaxial strain causes discrete polarisation switching in hBN B-centre emitters through a strain-induced Jahn–Teller effect. The findings could support deterministic alignment of emitters with nanophotonic cavities for on-chip quantum technologies.

articles.title_original: Sustainable Machining of Al7075-T6 Alloy Using MXene/h-BN Hybrid Nanolubricant and Plasma-Coated Tool: Surface Integrity, Wear Mechanisms, and Parameter Optimization
articles.title_en: MXene/h-BN Nanolubrication Improves Sustainable Machining of Al7075-T6
articles.excerpt_original: This study evaluates cutting force, microhardness, cutting temperature, chip morphology, specific cutting energy and tool wear under dry cutting, minimum quantity lubrication (MQL) and nano minimum quantity lubrication (NMQL) environments. Mahua oil mixed with hybrid nanoparticles (h-BN and MXene) was employed to study machining performance of aerospace alloy. Adding h-BN nanoparticles to mahua oil improved the cutting fluid's physicochemical, thermal, and lubricating properties. Two cutting speeds, 200 and 250 m/min, were utilized while keeping a constant feed rate of 0.12 mm/rev and a depth of cut (DOC) 1 mm. Findings showed that dry cutting produced the highest cutting forces, cutting temperature, and high tool wear than MQL and NMQL because of high friction and insufficient heat dissipation at the tool-chip contact. Scanning electron microscopy (SEM) investigation demonstrated built-upedge (BUE), flank wear and plastic deformation under dry environments. The implementation of the hybrid nanofluid strategy significantly reduced specific cutting energy to 17.17 KJ compared to specific cutting energy 21 KJ under dry mode. NMQL achieved around a 62% reduction in tool wear compared to dry cutting and around a 40% reduction compared to MQL. In all, NMQL was shown to be the best performing and sustainable cooling-lubrication approach for improving machinability while turning Al7075-T6 alloy.
articles.summary_en: An academic study found that nano minimum quantity lubrication using mahua oil with MXene and h-BN nanoparticles reduced specific cutting energy and tool wear when machining Al7075-T6 aerospace alloy. The approach delivered approximately 62% lower tool wear than dry cutting and 40% lower wear than conventional minimum quantity lubrication.

articles.title_original: High‐Performance Transistors beyond the 1‐nm CMOS Node: From Channel Materials and Three‐Dimensional Architectures to Cross‐Layer Co‐optimization
articles.title_en: Transistor Scaling Beyond the 1-nm CMOS Node
articles.excerpt_original: ABSTRACT Continuous complementary metal–oxide–semiconductor scaling has driven successive gains in computing performance, energy efficiency, and integration density. Beyond the 1‐nm node, however, lateral shrinkage yields diminishing returns as channel electrostatics and transport, parasitic resistance and capacitance, and lithographic cost cease to scale together. This review examines scaling across materials, devices, cells, and systems. At the channel level, SiGe‐ and Ge‐rich channels, two‐dimensional semiconductors, aligned carbon nanotubes, and III–V nanowires provide mobility, injection velocity, or electrostatic advantages, but require low‐resistance contacts, controlled dielectric interfaces, polarity control, uniformity, and wafer‐scale integration. At the device and cell levels, highly stacked and vertical‐channel gate‐all‐around field‐effect transistors (FETs) increase footprint‐normalized current or decouple gate length from lateral footprint, while complementary FETs and Flip FETs increase complementary‐device density and enable dual‐sided routing; source/drain resistance, capacitance, buried‐device access, high‐aspect‐ratio fabrication, and thermal budgets remain limiting. At the chip and system levels, system–technology co‐optimization, represented by TSMC's system‐integration roadmap and Huawei's τ‐Scaling and LogicFolding, redirects optimization from transistor density toward time and energy for useful computation. Connecting these levels within a materials–process–device–circuit–system framework establishes whether materials and vertical architectures deliver real current, density, and time benefits or merely transfer bottlenecks across the stack.
articles.summary_en: This review assesses channel materials, vertical transistor architectures, and system-level co-optimization strategies for scaling beyond 1-nm CMOS. It identifies contacts, dielectric interfaces, fabrication complexity, thermal budgets, and integration uniformity as key barriers to realizing practical performance and density gains.

articles.title_original: Quantum transport reveals spin-glass correlations in a two-dimensional network of TbPc 2 single-molecule magnets grafted on graphene.
articles.title_en: Graphene Network Shows Spin-Glass Correlations from Magnetic Molecules
articles.excerpt_original: The low temperature magnetoresistance of graphene functionalized by an array of magnetic Terbium Phthalocyanines molecules is found to exhibit a magnetic field-dependent 1/f noise, along with universal conductance fluctuations (UCFs) typical of a mesoscopic phase-coherent sample. A thorough analysis of the magnetic field, temperature and chemical potential dependence of this 1/f noise and UCFs reveals that long range, 2D Ising spin-glass like, magnetic correlations are induced in graphene through exchange interactions between the magnetic molecules and charge carriers in graphene. These experiments show that graphene functionalized with organic molecules constitutes a versatile platform for the investigation of magnetic phase transitions in two dimensions.
articles.summary_en: Researchers found that graphene functionalized with terbium phthalocyanine molecules exhibits magnetic-field-dependent 1/f noise and universal conductance fluctuations. The results indicate long-range two-dimensional spin-glass-like correlations, positioning the platform for fundamental studies of magnetic phase transitions.

articles.title_original: Composition-Dependent Structure and Electrochemical Performance of MXene/Polypyrrole/ZnO Ternary Nanocomposites for Supercapacitor Electrodes
articles.title_en: MXene/Polypyrrole/ZnO Nanocomposites Improve Supercapacitor Performance
articles.excerpt_original: The development of high-performance supercapacitor electrodes requires optimizing charge storage, electron transport, and active-site accessibility. In this study, MXene/polypyrrole/zinc oxide (MXene/PPy/ZnO) ternary nanocomposites were fabricated through in situ polymerization followed by hydrothermal synthesis, systematically varying PPy content and ZnO precursor concentration. Structural and morphological analyses revealed that composite composition influenced ZnO crystal growth and distribution, with excessive precursor concentrations promoting aggregation. M-3P-1Z exhibited uniformly distributed ZnO nanorods and the lowest charge-transfer resistance (0.4713 Ω), achieving the highest CV-derived specific capacitance of 888.01 F g−1 at 1 mV s−1. In contrast, M-1P-0.5Z, featuring ZnO nanorods with an aspect ratio of 10.1, achieved the highest GCD-derived specific capacitance of 1548.75 F g−1 at 0.1 A g−1 and a maximum estimated energy density of 161.2 Wh kg−1 at 160 W kg−1. Furthermore, its specific capacitance increased from 56.3 to 306.25 F g−1 after 1000 cycles at 5 A g−1, indicating progressive electrochemical activation. These findings highlight the importance of balancing ZnO morphology, accessible charge-storage sites, and MXene/PPy conductive networks, providing a composition-guided strategy for developing ternary nanocomposite electrodes with improved electrochemical energy storage performance.
articles.summary_en: Researchers optimized MXene/polypyrrole/zinc oxide nanocomposite composition for supercapacitor electrodes. The best formulations achieved reported specific capacitances of up to 1,548.75 F g−1 and an estimated energy density of 161.2 Wh kg−1, highlighting the role of ZnO morphology and conductive-network balance.

articles.title_original: Antibacterial heterostructures of fullerenes and boron-containing nanoparticles
articles.title_en: Antibacterial Heterostructures Combine Fullerenes with Boron Nanoparticles
articles.summary_en: Academic research examines antibacterial heterostructures composed of fullerenes and boron-containing nanoparticles. The work is relevant to nanomaterial-based biomedical applications, although the available information does not specify performance or deployment stage.

articles.title_original: Metal-Free Spin Crossover Through Nitrogen-Intercalated Graphene Under Pressure
articles.title_en: Theoretical Metal-Free Spin Crossover in Nitrogen-Intercalated Graphene
articles.excerpt_original: Spin crossover (SCO) phenomena, in which the spin state of an atom changes due to an external stimulus, have been the subject of ongoing research interest to this day. However, the considered atoms have been limited to transition metals like iron or cobalt. In this theoretical study, we show for the first time that external pressure can cause a nitrogen atom, i.e., a non-metal, to transit from a high spin (HS) to a low spin (LS) configuration. This nitrogen atom is located between two graphene sheets (N@Graphene) to mediate anisotropic pressure, serving as a proof-of-principle system on a periodic density functional theory (DFT) level. With increasing pressure, the distance between nitrogen and the graphene sheets decreases, leading to a SCO at a pressure below 5 GPa. To understand more about the mechanism behind the SCO, a finite model system, N@Circumcoronene, was constructed to allow the application of various electronic structure analysis tools for finite systems. These tools confirm that the SCO is the result of a closed-shell-dominated interaction in the sandwich structure. This work introduces a promising basis for the realization of a new class of materials with pressure-sensitive SCO involving main group atoms.
articles.summary_en: Density functional theory predicts that nitrogen confined between graphene sheets can switch from high-spin to low-spin under pressures below 5 GPa. The result suggests a basis for pressure-sensitive spin-crossover materials using non-metal atoms, but remains theoretical.

articles.title_original: Degradation of Rhodamine B by Magnetic Graphene Oxide-Activated Peroxymonosulfate

RhB degradation performance was investigated under varying conditions including MGO dosage, PMS concentration, pH, and initial RhB concentration. The effects of coexisting anions [chloride ions ( Cl − ), sulfate ions ( SO 4 2 − ), bicarbonate ions ( HCO 3 − ), and carbonate ions ( CO 3 2 − )] on degradation efficiency were examined. Results indicate that under optimal conditions (0.03 g MGO, 1 mmol / L PMS, pH = 7, 110 mg / L RhB), a 98.3% degradation efficiency was achieved after 400 min of agitation. articles.summary_en: Researchers synthesized magnetic graphene oxide by immobilizing iron on graphene oxide, forming Fe–O bonds and increasing surface area and pore volume. Under reported optimal conditions, the material achieved 98.3% Rhodamine B degradation after 400 minutes, supporting potential use in advanced water-treatment oxidation processes.

articles.title_original: Interfacial Organization and Direction-Dependent Transport of Hydrocarbons in Graphene Slit Pores
articles.title_en: Study Maps Hydrocarbon Transport in Graphene Slit Pores
articles.excerpt_original: Hydrocarbon transport in nanopores depends on the spatial organization of the confined fluid. We investigate this relationship through molecular dynamics simulations of methane, benzene, and n-octane between fixed graphene sheets, varying temperature and pore width. Density profiles and orientational distributions are combined with lateral mobility and wall-to-wall exchange to characterize structure and motion in interfacial and interior populations. Surface-aligned benzene layers sustain appreciable lateral mobility, whereas tightly confined n-octane exhibits strongly suppressed translation despite orientational rearrangement. Methane displays weak regional contrast in lateral mobility in the wider pores. In wide-pore benzene, molecular redistribution between interfacial and interior environments and orientational broadening accompany a nonmonotonic thermal response of lateral mobility. Lateral translation and wall-to-wall exchange exhibit distinct dependences on pore width, reflecting different constraints on motion within adsorbed layers and transfer between interfaces. These results connect adsorption and molecular packing to spatially heterogeneous transport and identify how molecular architecture and pore geometry shape motion along the interfaces and across the pore.
articles.summary_en: Molecular-dynamics simulations show that hydrocarbon mobility and exchange between graphene interfaces depend strongly on molecular structure, temperature, and pore width. The findings could inform graphene-based nanopore designs for hydrocarbon separation and transport, although no device or commercial validation is reported.

articles.title_original: Photoelectrochromism of Semiconductor Heterojunction All‐Solid‐State Electrochromic Device
articles.title_en: All-Solid-State Semiconductor Device Enables Photoelectrochromic Optical Modulation
articles.excerpt_original: ABSTRACT Photoelectrochromism, combining autonomous environmental adaptation of photochromism with accurate control of electrochromism in one system, is a desired strategy for dynamic optical modulation. Conventional photoelectrochromic systems are limited by poor photochemical stability and electrochemical reversibility, which results from the incompatibility between photogenerated carriers and electrochemical doping equilibrium. Herein, instead of an electrochemical system, a semiconductor heterojunction composed of the C‐rich carbon nitride conjugated polymer (CPCN) and TiO 2 nanocrystals with the configuration of TiO 2 /CPCN/TiO 2 is used to fabricate an all‐solid‐state electrochromic device. The working mechanisms, performances, and enabled functionalities are investigated and evaluated. The device exhibits high optical modulation contrast exceeding 80%, rapid coloration response within 1 s as well as great stability, and achieves light‐triggered functionalities, such as light‐controlled transmittance modulation, high‐resolution photochromic image display and photo‐writing.
articles.summary_en: Researchers developed an all-solid-state electrochromic device using a TiO₂/carbon nitride conjugated polymer/TiO₂ heterojunction. The device reportedly delivers over 80% optical contrast, sub-second coloration, stability, and light-triggered display and photo-writing functions.

articles.title_original: Aligned graphene frameworks enabling high-thermal-conductivity phase-change thermal storage composites
articles.title_en: Review Examines Aligned Graphene Frameworks for Thermal Storage
articles.excerpt_original: Phase change materials (PCMs) offer high thermal storage density, but their low intrinsic thermal conductivity limits rapid thermal charging and discharging. Incorporating thermally conductive fillers can enhance heat transfer but generally reduces latent heat capacity, creating a trade-off between thermal conductivity and energy storage density. Constructing continuous and aligned heat-transfer pathways offers a promising strategy to alleviate this trade-off by improving thermal conductivity at lower filler loadings. Graphene, with its high in-plane thermal conductivity, is an attractive building block for such pathways. However, the effective thermal conductivity of graphene-based phase change composites (PCCs) remains far lower than the theoretical value owing to multiple limiting factors. Focusing on this challenge, this review adopts an integrated multiscale analytical framework to explore how the intrinsic thermal transport potential of graphene can be more effectively utilized in aligned graphene-based PCCs. It first examines graphene’s intrinsic thermal transport properties and their influencing factors, then systematically summarizes aligned assembly strategies and introduces a loading-normalized metric for supplementary assessment of graphene utilization efficiency. Furthermore, strategies for reducing thermal resistance at intersheet junctions and graphene–matrix interfaces are discussed to address another key limitation of macroscopic thermal transport. Recent applications in energy storage and conversion and advanced thermal management are also reviewed. Finally, it highlights key challenges and future research directions for improving thermal performance, ensuring long-term reliability, and enabling scalable fabrication.
articles.summary_en: A review analyzes aligned graphene pathways in phase-change composites to improve thermal conductivity while limiting filler loading and latent-heat losses. It identifies intersheet and graphene–matrix thermal resistance, scalability, and long-term reliability as key challenges for energy-storage and thermal-management applications.

articles.title_original: MXene conductive hydrogel for uniform electric field wound healing
articles.title_en: MXene–EGaIn hydrogel patch enables electric-field wound healing
articles.excerpt_original: Flexible conductive materials show considerable potential for tissue engineering and regenerative medicine owing to their favorable mechanical properties, biocompatibility, and electrical characteristics. This study introduces a sequentially bridged, flexible three-layer composite composed of eutectic gallium-indium alloy (EGaIn), MXene, and hydrogel (EMH). This innovative conductive patch exhibits a spatially uniform electric-field distribution and stable electrical performance. The EGaIn layer provides exceptional conductivity, while MXene serves as an active capacitive layer with a high surface area and redox-active sites, facilitating efficient charge storage and redistribution. The synergy between MXene and EGaIn ensures rapid and uniform charge delivery, thereby enhancing electrochemical performance. The hyaluronic acid/polyacrylic acid double-network hydrogel (HPD) imparts remarkable tissue adhesion and mechanical compliance to the EMH patch. Significantly, the EMH demonstrates three times the capacitance compared to the EGaIn-hydrogel (EH), features metallic conductivity (775000 S/m) for swift charge transfer, and maintains stable cycling with less than 2Ω resistance at 235% strain. Its integrated design promise’s reliability under extreme deformation (up to 290% strain), effectively merging MXene’s charge storage capabilities with EGaIn’s strain-tolerant conduction. As an electronic wound dressing, the EMH patch significantly promotes tissue regeneration by facilitating endogenous current conduction that suppresses inflammation and stimulates cell proliferation, thereby enhancing epithelialization and vascularization. This capacitor-integrated layered design offers a promising bioelectronic approach for electric-field-modulated tissue regeneration.
articles.summary_en: Researchers developed a flexible three-layer wound dressing combining MXene, eutectic gallium–indium alloy and a hyaluronic acid/polyacrylic acid hydrogel. The patch provides uniform electric-field delivery, high conductivity and strain tolerance, while promoting tissue regeneration in the reported study.

articles.title_original: Multiscale Intercalation Strategies for Reconstructing Lamellar MXene Membranes
articles.title_en: Review Examines Intercalation Strategies for MXene Membranes
articles.excerpt_original: Abstract Lamellar MXene membranes, constructed by stacking MXene nanosheets to form two-dimensional nanochannels with ultrafast transport and sieving ability, have emerged as a promising platform for molecular and ionic separations as well as osmotic energy harvesting. However, the performance of these MXene membranes is often constrained by swelling-induced unstable nanochannels and monotonous chemistry environments within nanochannels. One of the most effective routes to these challenges lies in the incorporation of functional intercalation matters into the confined nanochannels of MXene, which not only orchestrate interlayer spacing and nanochannel chemistry but also improve stability by forming multiple interactions with neighboring nanosheets. Over the past decade, a series of multiscale intercalation matters have been designed and explored, mainly spanning from ions to small molecules, polymers, and nanomaterials. Despite significant achievements, a timely and comprehensive review that systematically elucidates how various multiscale intercalation matters reconstruct MXene membranes is missing. In this review, we discuss recent advances in intercalation strategies for lamellar MXene membranes, categorized by the chemical nature and dimensionality of the intercalating matters. We underscore their critical roles in modulating both the structural and chemical features of nanochannels, and we systematically analyze the corresponding effects on transport behavior and separation performance. Finally, some key unresolved challenges and future directions are highlighted to guide the design and synthesis of high-performance lamellar MXene membranes.
articles.summary_en: The review surveys ions, molecules, polymers and nanomaterials used to stabilize MXene lamellar membranes and tune their nanochannel spacing and chemistry. It assesses impacts on molecular and ionic separation, transport behavior and osmotic energy harvesting, while identifying remaining design challenges.

articles.title_original: Cu-Doped Intercalation-Engineered 2D ZIF-8/alk-MXene Heterostructure: A High-Performance Synergistic Adsorbent for Efficient Tetracycline Removal from Wastewater
articles.title_en: Cu-Doped ZIF-8/MXene Adsorbent Removes Tetracycline from Wastewater
articles.excerpt_original: Abstract The safe disposal of high-concentration antibiotic wastewater from medical, livestock and aquaculture sectors is critical to ecological security and public health. Herein, a Cu-doped ZIF-8/alk-MXene heterostructure with a well-defined intercalation structure and ultrahigh adsorption capacity for tetracycline in aquaculture wastewater was rationally fabricated via in-situ growth and post-modification. This heterostructured material (Cu-ZIF-8/alk-MXene) was fabricated via in-situ growth of two-dimensional ZIF-8 nanosheets within the intercalated structure of alkalized MXene (alk-MXene) followed by Cu doping, which synergized the electron-metal-support interactions (EMSI) induced by Cu dopants and the inherent structural merits of alk-MXene. Impressively, the Cu-ZIF-8/alk-MXene adsorbent achieves a remarkably boosted TC adsorption capacity in wastewater through the synergy of electrostatic attraction, metal coordination and π-π interaction. The Pseudo-second-order kinetic and Langmuir isotherm fitting further verify that the adsorption process is mainly controlled by chemical adsorption and follows a monolayer adsorption pattern. The composite delivers a Langmuir maximum TC adsorption capacity of 1631.1 mg·g -1 , with stable performance across pH 4-10 and initial TC concentrations of 10-200 mg·L -1 . It also shows excellent reusability: after five consecutive adsorption-desorption cycles, the adsorbent retains approximately 1283 mg·g -1 of TC uptake, corresponding to ~78.7% of its initial capacity, and exhibits strong anti-interference ability against coexisting ions in complex water matrices. DFT calculations further verify that the synergistic TC adsorption arises from the combined effects of metal coordination, electrostatic attraction and π-π interaction. This
articles.summary_en: Researchers developed a copper-doped ZIF-8/alkalized MXene heterostructure for tetracycline removal from wastewater. The adsorbent achieved a reported maximum capacity of 1,631.1 mg/g, retained about 78.7% of its initial uptake after five cycles, and remained effective across pH 4–10.

The code computes photon-shot-noise detection limits of T1 relaxometry with boron-vacancy (VB−) ensembles in few-layer hBN and with shallow nitrogen-vacancy ensembles in diamond. The folder figures/data holds one CSV file per figure panel or table; README.md lists the run order and the file contents.
