articles.summary_en: A review assesses polymer composites containing graphene and other two-dimensional fillers for reducing hydrogen permeation in pipelines, storage vessels, coatings, liners, and films. It highlights improved diffusion tortuosity while identifying nanosheet alignment, interfacial stability, oxidation resistance, scalable manufacturing, and long-term durability as key challenges.

articles.title_original: Electronic and optoelectronic devices
articles.title_en: Twisted 2D Heterostructures Enable Tunable Electronic and Optoelectronic Devices
articles.excerpt_original: Two-dimensional materials and their vdW HSs have emerged as a transformative platform for next-generation electronic and optoelectronic devices [1]. Unlike conventional bulk semiconductors, these materials possess atomically thin thickness, dangling-bond-free surfaces, and exceptional electrostatic tunability, enabling precise control over charge, spin, and excitonic degrees of freedom [2]. Their reduced dimensionality leads to enhanced quantum confinement, strong Coulomb interactions, and highly efficient light-matter coupling, all of which are critical for advanced device functionalities [3]. A defining advantage of vdW HSs lies in their ability to combine dissimilar materials without the constraints of lattice matching that limit traditional epitaxial growth. This freedom allows the creation of atomically sharp, clean interfaces with tailored band alignments, type-I, type-II, or type-III, each enabling distinct device operations such as carrier confinement, charge separation, or tunneling transport. As a result, vdW assembly enables the rational design of multifunctional devices by stacking materials with complementary properties, effectively creating artificial solids with engineered electronic structures. The introduction of twist as an additional degree of freedom has further revolutionized this field. Twisted heterostructures (t-HSs) give rise to moiré superlattices, where periodic modulation of the atomic registry generates long-range potential landscapes. These moiré patterns fundamentally reconstruct the electronic band structure, leading to the formation of minibands, flat bands, and spatially varying electronic states. Consequently, carrier dynamics in these systems can be tuned not only by material composition and external fields but also by the twist angle
articles.summary_en: Research describes how van der Waals heterostructures combine dissimilar two-dimensional materials to engineer band alignment, carrier transport, and light–matter interactions. Twist-controlled moiré patterns provide an additional route to tune minibands and electronic states for next-generation devices.

articles.title_original: BNNT/SWCNT/PDMS Composites for Dual Electromagnetic Interference and Neutron Shielding
articles.title_en: BNNT/SWCNT–PDMS Composite Combines EMI and Neutron Shielding
articles.excerpt_original: Abstract A lightweight and thin material that could simultaneously attenuate both electromagnetic interference (EMI) and neutron radiation is urgently required for advanced electronic and aerospace applications. In this study, we report a composite comprising BNNT/SWCNT/PDMS to achieve synergistic EMI and neutron-shielding performance. Resulting in excellent EMI shielding effectiveness, reaching approximately 45 dB at a BNNT: SWCNT ratio of 1:9, while maintaining appreciable performance even at low SWCNT content. In addition, the composite exhibits a neutron attenuation coefficient of 0.282 mm-1. Furthermore, structural characterization confirmed the effective integration of boron nitride nanotubes (BNNTs) and single-walled carbon nanotubes (SWCNTs), with enhanced interlayer stacking observed in the hybrid system. These results present a lightweight and multi-shielding composite for next-generation shielding material.
articles.summary_en: Researchers report a lightweight BNNT/SWCNT–PDMS composite delivering approximately 45 dB electromagnetic-interference shielding and a neutron attenuation coefficient of 0.282 mm⁻¹. The hybrid material targets dual-use electronic and aerospace shielding applications.

articles.title_original: Studies of indium - A 3 B 6 layered crystal surface nanosystems’ formation by fractal dimension kinetics
articles.title_en: Fractal Kinetics of Indium Nanostructures on Layered Semiconductor Crystals
articles.excerpt_original: We investigate the growth kinetics of indium nanostructures on A3B6 layered chalcogenide crystals (In4Se3, InTe) surfaces using STM-based fractal surface analysis. By applying the Flooding method to STM images of different resolutions, we quantify the evolution of fractal dimension during indium deposition and secondary solid-state dewetting. The results reveal resolution-dependent signatures of Gibbs–Thomson–driven nanostructure coarsening, height-distribution effects, and distinct growth regimes governed by substrate anisotropy. Comparative analysis across macro and nano scale STM areas demonstrates that fractal metrics efficiently capture surface complexity and reliably characterize hetero nanostructure formation on 2D semiconductor templates.
articles.summary_en: Researchers used scanning tunneling microscopy and fractal-dimension analysis to study indium nanostructure growth on In4Se3 and InTe layered chalcogenide surfaces. The findings identify resolution-dependent coarsening and substrate-anisotropy effects, supporting characterization of heterostructure formation on two-dimensional semiconductor templates.

articles.title_original: 5G CATS: 5G-Based Cryptographic Authorization Against Trafficking of Semiconductor Devices
articles.title_en: 5G System Verifies Semiconductor Device Location to Enforce Export Controls
articles.excerpt_original: Enforcing export controls on AI accelerators requires verifying where a chip operates after deployment. Round-trip time measurements can bound a chip's distance from a trusted landmark, but any jitter in honest replies forces the verifier to loosen its timeout, giving an attacker slack to relay traffic over fiber from a restricted region. Prior approaches either cross the untrusted host stack or rely on noisy power-line channels that inflate this slack. We present 5G CATS, a location certification system that pairs a co-packaged 5G radio, cryptographic engine, and hardware interlock on the GPU package with 5G Ultra-Reliable Low-Latency Communication (URLLC) base stations. Terminating the radio link inside the package removes the host software, PCIe fabric, and baseboard management controller from the verification path. We map an authenticated challenge-response protocol onto 5G's slot structure, replace permanent key erasure with short-lived execution leases, and specify a cross-check of the chip's reported serving cell against the carrier's own attachment records. In ns-3 and 5G-LENA simulations of an unloaded cell, our URLLC-based radio profile narrows the 99.9th percentile round-trip spread to 2.60 ms, more than ten times narrower than default 5G. A tracer rejects every round of a fiber relay from 300 km, against 2,000 km for default 5G. Against a 3,000 km attacker, a tracer stays safe at up to 1,410 km from the chip, against at most 619 km for PowerCATS's published model, while default 5G is never safe.
articles.summary_en: Researchers propose 5G CATS, which combines a co-packaged 5G radio, cryptographic engine, and hardware interlock to certify where AI accelerators operate after deployment. Simulations indicate substantially tighter timing bounds and improved rejection of long-distance fiber-relay attacks than default 5G or prior approaches.

articles.title_original: Tunable quasi-BIC-enhanced graphene metasurface absorber
articles.title_en: Tunable quasi-BIC graphene metasurface achieves 99.9% absorption
articles.excerpt_original: Abstract Graphene has garnered extensive attention due to its unique optoelectronic properties. However, its relatively weak light–matter interaction results in low absorption, limiting its applications in optoelectronic devices. The emergence of bound states in the continuum (BICs) offers a novel approach to enhancing light–matter interactions. However, most current research focuses on enhancing light absorption of graphene by exciting symmetry-protected quasi-BICs, which usually rely on asymmetric metasurface designs and thus increase fabrication complexity. In this paper, we design a graphene-based accidental quasi-BIC metasurface absorber. By exciting accidental quasi-BICs, we significantly enhance the absorption of monolayer graphene. We achieve an absorption as high as 99.9% using the proposed structure. We can also actively tune the quasi-BIC by modifying the graphene Fermi energy and geometric parameters. This work may offer novel insights into enhancing light absorption in graphene and other two-dimensional materials, and provide a reference for designing optoelectronic devices such as modulators, photodetectors, and optical sensors.
articles.summary_en: IOP Publishing researchers designed a graphene-based accidental quasi-bound-state-in-the-continuum (quasi-BIC) metasurface absorber that reportedly reaches 99.9% absorption in monolayer graphene. The tunable design could support graphene optoelectronic devices including modulators, photodetectors and optical sensors, while avoiding the asymmetric structures often used for quasi-BIC excitation.

articles.title_original: Micro-trench measurement of selective boron deposition during boron powder dropper operation in DIII-D
articles.title_en: Micro-Trench Study Measures Selective Boron Deposition in DIII-D Divertor
articles.excerpt_original: Abstract The selective boron (B) deposition rate is reported as measured using the micro-trench method in the DIII-D divertor during deuterium (D) H-mode outer strike point (OSP) sweeping plasma discharges with B powder injection via the impurity powder dropper (IPD). The selective deposition is defined as a result of B deposition and impurity sputtering (deposited B sputtered by B ions or other impurity ion species) in a micro-scale region geometrically shadowed from direct fuel/D + ion bombardment. To perform this work, micro-trenches 32 μ m × 32 μ m × 4 μ m deep were fabricated on a single-crystal silicon sample. The sample was exposed to DIII-D H-mode ‘cleaning’ plasma discharges with D fueling and OSP sweeping via the divertor material evaluation system (DiMES). The IPD injected B powder at rates of 5–20 mg s −1 during 2–5 s of H-mode plasmas in multiple discharges, adding up to 0.4 g injected in total. Injected B powders were ablated, ionized, and transported to PFC surfaces. Post-mortem analysis revealed that impurity deposition concentrated in a D + ion shadowed area on the micro-trench floor, while no B deposition was observed outside of the micro-trench, which implied that net impurity deposition can be significantly enhanced by rough micro-structures on PFC surfaces, i.e. selective deposition. An energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy (EDS) analysis detected impurity deposition containing B, carbon, oxygen, and silicon. Combining the impurity deposition height profile measured by atomic force microscopy and the relative B concentration profiles measured by EDS, we determined the selective B deposition thickness of ∼25 nm in the diverter region. The measured B deposition thickness agreed with a mass balance analysis to within half the magnitude when the B impuri
articles.summary_en: Experiments in DIII-D’s H-mode plasma measured approximately 25 nm of selective boron deposition in micro-trenches exposed to injected boron powder. The findings indicate that rough, fuel-ion-shadowed structures can enhance impurity retention on plasma-facing components, informing fusion-materials and divertor-surface studies.

articles.title_original: Evidence of anomalous Hall crystals in moiré rhombohedral graphene
articles.title_en: Evidence for anomalous Hall crystals in moiré rhombohedral graphene
articles.excerpt_original: An anomalous Hall crystal (AHC) is a quantum state of matter, in which spontaneous electron crystallization leads to a quantized Hall effect without a magnetic field. The state can emerge in materials with strong Coulomb interaction and large Berry curvatures, such as few-layer rhombohedral graphene. Although the idea of AHCs has been invoked to explain some of the observed Chern insulators in moiré rhombohedral graphene (mRG), direct experimental evidence of AHCs has been missing so far. Here, we report experimental evidence of AHCs in hole-doped mRG through combined electrical transport and noise measurements. We identify a series of distinct Chern insulators spanning a broad and continuous range of doping densities incommensurate with the underlying moiré lattice; the states exhibit current-induced broadband noise and memory effects as well as pronounced gate hysteresis. Systematic magnetic field, temperature and gate dependence studies further support the emergence of a spontaneously charge-ordered state that acts as a parental state for the observed Chern insulators. The absence of Chern insulators at nearby integer fillings also distinguishes the observed state from the reported reentrant or extended quantum (anomalous) Hall states. Altogether, our results establish experimental evidence of AHCs in mRG and open the door for further exploration of the collective dynamics in this new state of matter.
articles.summary_en: Experiments combining electrical transport and noise measurements provide evidence for spontaneously charge-ordered anomalous Hall crystals in hole-doped moiré rhombohedral graphene. The findings identify a broad range of Chern-insulating states and could advance research into correlated quantum electronic phases.

articles.title_original: MXenes-based heterostructures versus carbon-based anodes for metal-ion batteries: performance benchmarks, commercial viability, and translation challenges
articles.title_en: MXene Anodes Benchmarking Against Graphene and Carbon Materials
articles.excerpt_original: MXenes and MXenes-based heterostructures have emerged as promising anodes for metal-ion batteries because of their high electrical conductivity, tunable surface chemistry, and layered structures. However, their practical competitiveness must be evaluated against commercially established carbon-based anodes rather than theoretical capacity alone. This review develops a translation-oriented benchmarking framework that evaluates pristine and functionalized MXenes and their heterostructures against graphite, hard carbon, graphene, and related carbonaceous anodes across four progressively realistic levels: intrinsic material properties, synthesized materials, electrode/full-cell performance, and commercial-readiness criteria. Particular attention is given to the persistent gap between computational predictions and experimental performance arising from idealized models, surface terminations, restacking, oxidation, electrolyte compatibility, and material variability. Heterostructure engineering for improving ion accessibility, conductivity, structural stability, and interfacial behavior is also assessed. By identifying both the performance advantages and persistent commercial limitations of MXenes-based systems, this review establishes practical design considerations to translate MXene anodes from laboratory-scale promise toward viable battery technologies.
articles.summary_en: A review compares MXene-based heterostructure anodes with graphite, hard carbon, graphene, and related carbon materials across performance and commercial-readiness criteria. It highlights translation barriers including restacking, oxidation, electrolyte compatibility, surface chemistry, and the gap between computational predictions and full-cell results.

articles.title_original: Anderson localization with single photons from a quantum emitter
articles.title_en: Single photons demonstrate Anderson localization in integrated photonics
articles.excerpt_original: Anderson localization of light is a fundamental emergent phenomenon in disordered systems. In arrays of coupled waveguides, it suppresses transport and causes photons to remain localized near the excitation site as coupling disorder increases. Here, we experimentally demonstrate Anderson localization using single photons emitted by a single-photon emitter in hexagonal boron nitride at room temperature. Despite the limited temporal coherence of the emitter, the photons undergo pronounced Anderson localization, evidenced by exponentially localized output intensity profiles in disordered waveguide lattices. Beyond the experimental demonstration, we develop a general theoretical framework for wave propagation in disordered tight-binding systems, showing that the configuration-averaged output intensity converges to a stationary spatial distribution at large propagation distances. In the case of off-diagonal disorder, this stationary profile is characterized by an effective localization length that exhibits a robust inverse-variance scaling with the disorder strength. These results establish defect-based room-temperature emitters as practical platforms for studying Anderson localization in integrated photonics and support their use in applications that exploit controlled disorder, including neuromorphic and quantum photonic architectures.
articles.summary_en: Researchers demonstrated Anderson localization using room-temperature single photons emitted by hexagonal boron nitride in disordered waveguide lattices. The findings support defect-based emitters for neuromorphic and quantum photonic architectures.

articles.title_original: Magnetic order tuning of excitons in the two-dimensional magnetic semiconductor CrCl_3 through strain
articles.title_en: Strain tunes excitonic magnetism in 2D CrCl₃ semiconductor
articles.excerpt_original: Magnon-exciton coupling provides an unprecedented opportunity for the optical tunability of spin information and, viceversa, for the magnetic control of the optical response. Few-layered magnets are an ideal platform for the experimental study of this coupling, in part due to the strong excitonic character of the optical response in (quasi-)two dimensions. Here, we demonstrate a strong dependence of the excitonic oscillator strength on the magnetic order in a monolayer of chromium trichloride CrCl$_3$. Solving an effective Bethe-Salpeter equation, we evaluate the changes in the excitonic response as the magnetic order switches from the ferromagnetic state to the antiferromagnetic state when strain is applied. Our results reveal an abrupt change in the spatial localization of the excitons across the transition, which translates into a strong shift and a change of the oscillator strength of the excitonic peaks. This suggests the possibility of using strain as a binary switch of the optical response in this material.
articles.summary_en: Researchers model how strain-driven transitions between ferromagnetic and antiferromagnetic order sharply alter exciton localization and oscillator strength in monolayer chromium trichloride. The findings suggest strain-controlled binary switching of optical responses for spin-based semiconductor technologies.

articles.title_original: Genesis of Nucleation Sites Dictates the Fate of 2D MoS2 Growth
articles.title_en: Nucleation Control Enables Scalable MoS₂ Growth
articles.excerpt_original: Scalable synthesis of two-dimensional (2D) transition metal dichalcogenides (TMDs) with atomic precision is critical for next-generation flexible electronics. Chemical vapor deposition is a primary strategy for the growth of 2D TMD films. The process, however, is difficult to control at large scales due to the strong interplay between time-dependent concentration gradients of the precursors, setup-specific fluid dynamics, and surface energetics. Here, we present a dual-channel reactor system that allows independent dynamic control over transition metal and chalcogen precursor dosages. This enables preprogrammed delivery of precursor partial pressures, effectively decoupling the chemical potentials governing nucleation and subsequent growth phases. This was demonstrated using molybdenum disulfide (MoS2) synthesis as an archetypical model system. By combining experiments and time-dependent fluid dynamics simulations, we have revealed that the genesis of nucleation sites, the local Mo/S ratio established during the fleeting initial nucleation event, decisively dictates the ultimate growth morphology. We demonstrate that near-stoichiometric S-rich conditions during both nucleation and growth stages favor 2D lateral expansion via heterogeneous surface reactions, whereas excessively S-rich conditions promote 3D growth through homogeneous gas-phase reactions. Furthermore, we show that the spatial limitations of traditional horizontal configurations, such as inherent concentration gradients and mass transport bottlenecks, are effectively bypassed using an optimized vertical substrate orientation. By thinning the boundary layer and stabilizing the chemical potential, this configuration shifts the rate-limiting step toward surface reaction kinetics. This dual approach of temporal
articles.summary_en: Researchers show that precursor ratios during the initial nucleation stage determine whether CVD-grown MoS₂ forms lateral 2D films or unwanted 3D structures. A dual-channel reactor and vertical substrate orientation reduce concentration gradients and transport bottlenecks, supporting more controllable scale-up for flexible electronics.

articles.title_original: Strain-enhanced high-order harmonic generation in boron nitride nanotubes
articles.title_en: Strain boosts high-order harmonic generation in boron nitride nanotubes
articles.excerpt_original: High-order harmonic generation (HHG) in pristine and transversely compressed boron nitride nanotubes (BNNTs) is investigated using extended multiband semiconductor Bloch equations (SBEs). At a transverse strain of −10%, the harmonic yield is enhanced by approximately two orders of magnitude relative to the pristine structure. The enhancement is dominated by the interband channel. Symmetry reduction activates or strengthens interband transition channels, and selectively suppressing these couplings substantially reduces the enhanced emission. The enhancement is most pronounced at low driving fields and persists over the investigated wavelength range. These results identify transverse compression as a means of controlling HHG in BNNTs.
articles.summary_en: Researchers report that 10% transverse compression enhances high-order harmonic generation in boron nitride nanotubes by approximately two orders of magnitude. The effect arises mainly from strengthened interband transitions enabled by symmetry reduction, suggesting strain control for nanoscale nonlinear optical and semiconductor devices.

articles.title_original: Research data supporting "Spontaneous Surface Charging and Janus Nature of the Hexagonal Boron Nitride–Water Interface"
articles.title_en: Machine-learning dataset models charging at the hBN–water interface
articles.excerpt_original: Input files (in .xyz format) used to develop the MACE machine learning potential (MLP) reported in this work. The dataset includes the training set (train.xyz), the test set (test.xyz), and the full dataset (input.xyz). Reference energies and forces were computed with CP2K using the revPBE-D3(0) functional. The dataset builds on training data from previous studies of the hBN–water interface and bulk water under various conditions. It was extended with configurations targeting the chemisorbed and physisorbed states of the OH⁻ ion, as well as OH⁻ in water layers farther from the hBN interface. To maintain charge neutrality without a homogeneous background charge, these configurations include an H₃O⁺ counterion placed far from the OH⁻, which also lets the model describe H₃O⁺. The dataset further includes pure water and neutral water containing protonic defects in a range of environments: the air–water interface, the hBN–water interface with varying water-layer thicknesses, and water confined between hBN sheets. A final round of active learning was performed to refine the model across these conditions.
articles.summary_en: Researchers released supporting data for a machine-learning potential describing water, hydroxide, and hydronium configurations at hexagonal boron nitride–water interfaces. The dataset covers adsorbed states, confined water, and protonic defects to study the interface’s spontaneous surface charging and Janus behavior.

articles.title_original: Cold-source field-effect transistor with type-III band-aligned HfS 2 /WTe 2 heterostructure
articles.title_en: HfS₂/WTe₂ heterostructure enables low-power cold-source transistor
articles.excerpt_original: The cold source field-effect transistor (CSFET) is promising for reducing power dissipation in integrated circuits by engineering the density of states at the injecting source. Existing CSFET designs utilizing Dirac-source metals or p-Metal-n stacks are challenged by Schottky barriers at the metal-semiconductor interface. In this work, a 2D WTe$_2$/HfS$_2$ heterojunction with type-III band alignment is proposed to be an excellent design of cold source and CSFET. The architecture has a high band-to-band transport mechanism by removing the detrimental Schottky barrier issues. Importantly, the proposed CSFET has the same channel barrier modulation principle as conventional MOSFET to enable a high on-state current. Using first-principles-based quantum transport modeling, we predict a very high $I_{\rm on}$/$I_{\rm off}$ ratio at $\sim$ 10$^{10}$, a low subthreshold swing below the thermal limit for a wide range of gate voltages, reaching as small as 41.3 mV/dec, at low source-drain bias $V_{DS}=0.3$ $\rm V$. These findings establish a design principles for next-generation low-power nanoelectronic switches leveraging 2D van der Waals heterostructures.
articles.summary_en: Researchers propose a type-III band-aligned HfS₂/WTe₂ heterojunction for cold-source field-effect transistors, addressing Schottky-barrier limitations in previous designs. Quantum-transport modeling predicts an on/off ratio of approximately 10¹⁰ and a subthreshold swing as low as 41.3 mV/dec at 0.3 V drain–source bias.

articles.title_original: Rippled graphene pores as fluidic memristive devices with synaptic and neuromorphic functionalities
articles.title_en: Rippled graphene pores enable scalable fluidic memristors
articles.excerpt_original: Abstract Nanofluidic memristive devices work with nanoscale pores (or channels) and ions dissolved in water, which harness the ionic memory effect aiming to store and process information. These devices share the same charge carriers as biological systems and bring hope for better emulating the neural functions and developing ionic circuits for neuromorphic applications. Specifically, theory and experiments suggest that nanoconfinement is essential for inducing a memory effect, which places a limit on the pore size to nm-scale or smaller. Such devices are, however, difficult to scale up with precision and operate with long-term stability. Here, we show that a micrometer size pore, generally expected to exhibit a linear ion transport, can display a pronounced memory effect, if its rim is wrapped by strongly curved and tightly stacked graphene. We attribute the observation to slow ion dynamics confined in the rippled graphene edges. The devices are easy to scale up and integrate into fluidic circuits. The memory effect is ion-selective and, crucially, exhibits long endurance, which enables reversible modification of the conductance states using programmable voltage spikes and various electrolytes over a long time, akin to biological synaptic plasticity. Thanks to this plasticity, our devices and their integrated circuits enable storing, transmitting and processing information with exceptionally high reliability, fidelity and accuracy, as evidenced by the effective processing of largescale and event-based information in the identification of both grayscale and color images, and in the real-time analysis of emulated neural signals. Our results highlight nanoscale morphology of the pore wall as an important parameter regulating ion transport, in addition to the well-documente
articles.summary_en: Researchers demonstrate micrometer-scale pores with rippled graphene edges that exhibit ion-selective, long-endurance memristive behavior. The devices support programmable conductance and integrated neuromorphic processing of images and neural signals, potentially easing scale-up of ionic computing circuits.

articles.title_original: Multifunctional APTES-SWCNTs/ILs@PEDOT:PSS/MXene composite film toward wearable sensing, electromagnetic protection and low-voltage Joule heating
articles.title_en: Multifunctional SWCNT–PEDOT:PSS/MXene Film Enables Wearable Sensing and EMI Protection
articles.summary_en: Researchers developed a composite film combining single-walled carbon nanotubes, ionic liquids, PEDOT:PSS and MXene for wearable sensing, electromagnetic-interference protection and low-voltage Joule heating. The study indicates potential for multifunctional flexible electronics and dual-use electromagnetic-shielding applications.

articles.title_original: Non‐Invasive Optical Inspection of Thermally Driven Interface State Evolution at Buried Metal–MoS 2 Contacts
articles.title_en: Optical method tracks thermal evolution of graphene-buffered MoS₂ contacts
articles.excerpt_original: ABSTRACT Van der Waals (vdW) metal contacts to two‐dimensional semiconductors promise efficient carrier extraction alongside long photocarrier lifetimes, yet how the buried interface evolves under back‐end‐of‐line thermal budgets remains difficult to track. Here, annealing‐dependent transient reflection spectroscopy is established as a device‐free optical readout of interface state evolution for transferred vdW Au, graphene‐buffered Au, and deposited semimetal Sb contacts on multilayer MoS 2 up to 400°C, correlated with cross‐sectional electron microscopy, photoelectron spectroscopy, and first‐principles calculations. As the Au–S separation contracts from 3.47 Å to 2.16 Å (into the bonding range) two distinct optical signatures emerge: reduction of the early‐time excitonic response from the first annealing step, consistent with strengthening extraction, and a picosecond capture channel that appears at 200°C, following thermally activated chemisorption whose hybridization‐induced gap states straddle the pinned Fermi level. At matched separation, the Sb interface forms comparable gap states that lie occupied below its Fermi level, explaining its nearly invariant response, whereas graphene delays the transformation by holding the metal away from the semiconductor. These results frame contact selection as a navigable trade‐off between carrier extraction and photocarrier lifetime and identify interlayer engineering and semimetal contacts as complementary routes to thermally robust 2D interfaces.
articles.summary_en: Researchers developed transient reflection spectroscopy to monitor buried metal–MoS₂ interface changes during annealing up to 400°C. Graphene interlayers delayed thermally activated interface transformation, highlighting interlayer engineering as a route to more stable 2D semiconductor contacts.

articles.title_original: Amplified Spontaneous Emission and Carrier Dynamics in Ruddlesden–Popper and Dion–Jacobson Quasi‐2D Perovskite
articles.title_en: HBr-Treated Quasi-2D Perovskites Enable Low-Threshold Green Lasers
articles.excerpt_original: ABSTRACT Ruddlesden–Popper (RP) and Dion–Jacobson (DJ) quasi‐2D perovskites exhibit disparate chemical bonds and structures due to distinct organic spacer cations, endowing them with distinctive physical properties. A more far‐reaching investigation of the fundamental structure–physical relation, including the carrier dynamics, is expected in these layered perovskites. The phase distribution, defect state density, and ultrafast dynamics of RP‐type perovskite (PA) 2 () 3 and DJ‐type perovskite (HDAD) () 3 were investigated by using transient absorption spectra. The DJ‐type perovskite exhibits a lower threshold amplified spontaneous emission (ASE); however, its Auger recombination is more severe than that of RP‐type perovskite. By adding a trace amount of HBr to the solvent during crystal growth, exciton–phonon coupling was inhibited, energy transfer was promoted, and the Auger recombination was suppressed. We ultimately chose the HBr‐treated HDAD quasi‐2D perovskite thin films, achieving a low ASE threshold and high‐performance single‐mode green lasers.
articles.summary_en: Researchers compared carrier dynamics and amplified spontaneous emission in Ruddlesden–Popper and Dion–Jacobson quasi-2D perovskites. HBr treatment suppressed Auger recombination and enabled thin-film single-mode green lasers with low ASE thresholds.

articles.title_original: A monoelemental ferroelectric semiconductor
articles.title_en: Two-dimensional selenium identified as a room-temperature ferroelectric semiconductor
articles.excerpt_original: Abstract The emergence of single‑element ferroelectricity beyond traditional compound ferroelectrics broadens the ranges of ferroelectric materials and enriches polarization mechanisms. However, all prior elemental ferroelectrics (e.g., Bismuth and Tellurium) are metals or semimetals with narrow bandgaps, causing large leakage current, low breakdown voltage, and poor device reliability, severely limiting their practical applications in low‑power electronics and neuromorphic computing. Here, we report the first discovery of robust room-temperature ferroelectricity in a monoelemental ferroelectric semiconductor, two‑dimensional selenium (Se) nanosheets. Unexpectedly, a strong dipole-interlocking coupling between in-plane and out-of-plane polarizations enables simultaneous switching of both components. This coupling is rarely observed outside α-In₂Se₃. Our findings not only overcome the long-standing limitations of metallic/semimetallic elemental ferroelectrics by introducing a semiconducting elemental ferroelectric (Se), but also establish Se as a highly promising material platform for future low-power, multi-terminal, and multimodal neuromorphic computing hardware.
articles.summary_en: Researchers report robust room-temperature ferroelectricity in two-dimensional selenium nanosheets, addressing leakage and reliability limitations associated with prior elemental ferroelectrics. The material could support low-power, multi-terminal and multimodal neuromorphic hardware, although practical device validation remains necessary.

articles.title_original: Technical Note TN-2026-HBN-02: Longitudinal Split-Wafer (Clamshell) Fabrication and Open-Surface ALD Protocol for h-BN Protective Linings in Ultra-High-Gradient PWFA Capillaries
articles.title_en: Open-surface ALD process proposed for h-BN-lined PWFA capillaries
articles.excerpt_original: This technical note details the Longitudinal Split-Wafer (Clamshell) Architecture and Open-Surface Atomic Layer Deposition (ALD) protocol for depositing 50.0 nm hexagonal Boron Nitride (h-BN) protective linings inside high-gradient Plasma Wakefield Accelerator (PWFA) capillary channels. This leaves the surface completely open during deposition, guaranteeing zero precursor depletion and uniform 50.0 nm h-BN atomic layer growth across the entire 1.0-meter channel length prior to optical contact fusion. articles.title_original: Applications of Directed Self-Assembly Lithography in Advanced Semiconductor Devices
articles.title_en: Review examines directed self-assembly lithography for advanced semiconductors
articles.excerpt_original: As semiconductor devices continue to scale down, conventional lithography technologies face increasingly severe challenges in resolution, stochastic defect control, and manufacturing cost. Block copolymer (BCP) directed self-assembly (DSA), which offers molecular-scale control over pattern formation and compatibility with existing lithographic processes, has emerged as a promising complementary nanopatterning technology for advanced semiconductor manufacturing. This review summarizes the microphase-separation mechanisms of DSA, major guiding strategies including graphoepitaxy and chemoepitaxy, and pattern-transfer techniques such as dry and wet etching and sequential infiltration synthesis (SIS). In terms of device applications, particular emphasis is placed on recent progress in DSA for Fin Field-Effect Transistor (FinFET) fin patterning, silicon nanostructures, high-density contact holes, memory devices, two-dimensional semiconductors, and Complementary Metal-Oxide-Semiconductor (CMOS) optoelectronic devices. Key challenges, including defect control, process-window optimization, pattern transfer, and wafer-scale manufacturing, are further discussed, together with future directions involving the integration of DSA with extreme ultraviolet (EUV) lithography, advanced etching, and data-driven process optimization. This review aims to outline the technological evolution of DSA from nanoscale self-assembly toward integration into advanced semiconductor manufacturing and to provide a reference for high-resolution patterning at advanced technology nodes.
articles.summary_en: The review assesses block copolymer directed self-assembly for nanoscale patterning in FinFETs, memory, two-dimensional semiconductors, and CMOS optoelectronics. It highlights defect control, pattern transfer, process integration, and potential combinations with EUV lithography and data-driven optimization.
