articles.title_original: Carbon-Isotope Labeling Rules Out Covalent Sulfur Addition to Graphene
articles.title_en: Carbon-Isotope Labeling Refutes Covalent Sulfur Bonding to Graphene
articles.excerpt_original: Abstract Covalent functionalization of graphene is commonly inferred from Raman spectroscopy, photoelectron spectroscopy, microscopy, and first-principles calculations. However, these methods may not distinguish bonding to the graphene lattice from the adsorption of carbon-containing reaction products. Here, we investigate this ambiguity using the gas-phase reaction of sulfur radicals with graphene as a case study. Sulfur treatment produces new Raman bands, substantial changes in the photoemission spectra, and surface compositions consistent with sulfur addition. Density functional theory calculations further show that these observations can be reproduced by a stable graphene episulfide structure in which sulfur bridges two lattice carbon atoms. A decisive control experiment using isotopically pure 13C graphene nevertheless rules out this assignment. Although the intrinsic graphene Raman bands undergo the expected isotope shifts, the characteristic reaction–product bands near 1260 and 1450 cm–1 remain unchanged. The carbon atoms contributing to these modes therefore originate from extrinsic species rather than from the graphene lattice. Detection of similar products on hexagonal boron nitride further supports the formation of organosulfur species in the gas phase, followed by their selective deposition on hydrophobic surfaces. These results show that an extensive agreement among conventional characterization methods and theoretical predictions can still lead to an incorrect structural assignment. Isotopically labeled graphene provides a direct and broadly applicable control for establishing whether carbon atoms in proposed functional groups originate from the graphitic lattice.
articles.summary_en: Researchers used isotopically pure 13C graphene to show that sulfur-treatment signals previously attributed to graphene-bound episulfides instead arise from extrinsic organosulfur species deposited on the surface. The study demonstrates that conventional spectroscopy and modeling can produce incorrect structural assignments without isotope-labeling controls.

articles.title_original: Functionalized Graphene-Lignosulfonate Hydrogel Cathode for Zn-Ion Hybrid Capacitors
articles.title_en: Functionalized Graphene–Lignosulfonate Cathode Boosts Zn-Ion Hybrid Capacitors
articles.excerpt_original: Abstract Cathode materials, being pivotal to the performance of Zn-ion hybrid capacitors (ZIHCs), have garnered significant attention and research. However, the simple physical combination of components often causes phase interfaces, thereby impeding the optimization of electrode material performance. Herein, a functionalized graphene-lignosulfonate hydrogel (FRGO-Lig) is developed by a simple hydrothermal process using graphene oxide (GO) and biomass lignosulfonate (Lig) as raw materials with p-phenylenediamine (PPD) as the functionalizing modifier. The high electroactivity of Lig and PPD components can provide high capacitance contribution. In addition, the amine groups of PPD can simultaneously react with the epoxy groups of GO to functionalize graphene and the phenolic units of Lig to connect graphene and Lig by the formed –NH– covalent bonds during the hydrothermal process. This is beneficial for eliminating the phase interfaces to further improve charge transfer efficiency and electrochemical performance. When used as a supercapacitor electrode, the specific capacitance of FRGO-Lig can reach 425.3 F g–1 at a high current density of 5 A g–1 and still maintain 297 F g–1 at 50 A g–1, demonstrating a high-rate performance of 69.8%. Notably, the assembled ZIHCs using FRGO-Lig as the cathode achieved a high specific capacitance of 342.7 F g–1 at 1 A g–1 and an excellent energy density of 129.6 Wh kg–1 at a power density of 825 W kg–1, showcasing favorable practical application potential in advanced energy storage devices.
articles.summary_en: Researchers developed a covalently connected graphene–lignosulfonate hydrogel cathode using p-phenylenediamine functionalization. The electrode delivered 342.7 F g−1 and 129.6 Wh kg−1 in zinc-ion hybrid capacitors, indicating strong high-rate energy-storage performance.

articles.title_original: Data and code for: Group-aware validation of machine learning for CO2 uptake on graphene oxide and reduced graphene oxide adsorbents: uncertainty, applicability domain and the limits of textural descriptors
articles.title_en: Dataset and models benchmark CO2 uptake on graphene oxide adsorbents
articles.excerpt_original: Curated literature dataset, analysis code, trained model and full results accompanying a manuscript submitted to Results in Engineering. The dataset contains 632 CO2 uptake measurements on graphene oxide (GO) and reduced graphene oxide (rGO) adsorbents from 26 screened publications (541 in-domain measurements from 23 publications), with textural descriptors (BET surface area, total pore volume), operating conditions (temperature, pressure), material class and source of every value. Surface-chemistry descriptors extracted from the source papers and an external test set (four independent publications, 32 measurements, plus a 4-point sensitivity set) are included. The two notebooks reproduce every table and figure of the paper and its Supplementary Information: group-aware validation (leave-one-publication-out, leave-multiple-groups-out, repeated grouped cross-validation), model selection, applicability domain, group-conformal prediction intervals, feature attribution and the external test. The final model (scikit-learn Extra Trees pipeline, 13 inputs) is provided with its applicability-domain thresholds and conformal half-width. Licences: data, trained model and results CC BY 4.0; code (notebooks and go_co2_analysis.py) MIT. See README.md for contents and reproduction steps.
articles.summary_en: Researchers released a curated dataset, code, trained model and results for predicting CO2 uptake on graphene oxide and reduced graphene oxide adsorbents. Group-aware validation and applicability-domain analysis highlight uncertainty and the limits of relying only on textural descriptors such as surface area and pore volume.

articles.title_original: Correlative nanoscale chemical imaging reveals delocalized Faradaic processes at isolated MXene flakes
articles.title_en: Nanoscale imaging reveals delocalized electrochemical reactions on MXene flakes
articles.excerpt_original: Abstract Two-dimensional transition metal carbides and nitrides (MXenes) combine an electrochemically active surface with high conductivity and hydrophilicity, which makes them a unique class of materials for electrochemical applications. While the pseudocapacitive behaviour of MXenes in acidic environments is relatively well understood on macroscale electrodes, intrinsic electrochemical phenomena occurring on single MXene flakes remain unclear. Here, we use scanning X-ray microscopy (SXM) to correlate the electronic structure of Ti 3 C 2 T x MXene flakes at the nanoscale with local electrochemical reactions triggered at the sub-flake level by scanning electrochemical cell microscopy (SECCM). For several proton-coupled electron transfer reactions, including electrochemical oxidation and the hydrogen evolution reaction, we demonstrate a delocalization of the reactions well beyond the MXene flake area in contact with the droplet cell. Furthermore, we show evidence of hydrogen storage on monolayer MXene flakes. This work highlights fundamental insights into the role of interfacial water on surface redox reactions.
articles.summary_en: Researchers used correlated scanning X-ray microscopy and scanning electrochemical cell microscopy to show that electrochemical reactions on Ti₃C₂Tₓ MXene extend beyond the flake area contacted by the electrolyte. The study also provides evidence of hydrogen storage in monolayer MXene flakes, offering fundamental insights relevant to electrochemical energy-storage materials.

articles.title_original: Etching-dependent structure and catalytic performance of Ti₃C₂Tₓ MXene for oxidative desulfurization of dibenzothiophene
articles.title_en: Etching route boosts MXene catalytic desulfurization performance
articles.excerpt_original: The synthesis route of MXenes plays a crucial role in determining their structural characteristics and catalytic performance. In this work, Ti₃C₂Tₓ MXenes synthesized via conventional hydrofluoric acid (HF) etching and a mild in-situ LiF/HCl etching route were comparatively evaluated as catalysts for the oxidative desulfurization (ODS) of dibenzothiophene (DBT) using tert-butyl hydroperoxide, without additional active-metal modification. Structural characterizations confirmed successful conversion of Ti₃AlC₂ MAX phase into Ti₃C₂Tₓ MXene through both etching methods. Compared with HF etching, LiF/HCl produced MXene with a larger interlayer spacing (1.21 nm), higher pore volume (0.027 cm 3 .g −1 ), and more pronounced oxygen-containing surface functionalities, despite its lower BET surface area (11.8 vs. 15.5 m 2 .g −1 ). These structural differences markedly influenced the ODS performance. Under optimum conditions (120 °C, O/S = 4, catalyst dosage = 0.25 g.L −1 ), the LiF/HCl-derived MXene achieved complete DBT removal, whereas HF-derived MXene and pristine Ti₃AlC₂ reached 84% and 25% removal, respectively. The catalyst retained 91% of its initial activity after five recycling, and GC–MS confirmed DBTO 2 as the final oxidation product. The superior performance of the LiF/HCl-derived MXene is attributed to its favorable interlayer structure and surface chemistry, highlighting controlled etching as an effective strategy for designing efficient MXene catalysts for ultra-deep ODS.
articles.summary_en: Researchers found that mild LiF/HCl etching produced Ti₃C₂Tₓ MXene with structural and surface-chemistry advantages over HF-etched material. The catalyst achieved complete dibenzothiophene removal, retained 91% activity after five cycles, and outperformed both HF-derived MXene and the precursor MAX phase.

articles.title_original: Interface-engineered CoMoN/MXene hybrids with enhanced discharge ion-transport characteristics for advanced supercapattery applications
articles.title_en: CoMoN/MXene Hybrid Improves Ion Transport in Supercapattery Electrodes
articles.excerpt_original: Abstract The development of advanced energy storage systems (ESSs) that integrate the high energy density of batteries with the high-power density of supercapacitors has attracted considerable attention. In this study, an interface-engineered cobalt molybdenum nitride (CoMoN)/Ti 3 C 2 T x MXene hybrid with a hierarchical nanosheet-stacked architecture (CMN5M) is reported for high-performance supercapattery applications. Electrochemical analyses reveal distinct ion storage behaviors in the pristine CoMoN and hybrid electrodes. Diffusion coefficient ( M D ) analysis based on galvanostatic intermittent titration technique (GITT) reveals distinct ion-transport characteristics during charging and discharging. Pristine CoMoN exhibits relatively higher apparent ion diffusivity during charging, whereas the CoMoN/MXene hybrid shows enhanced apparent ion transport during discharge. These differences suggest that the conductive MXene framework and engineered interfaces facilitate ion transport in the hybrid electrode, with possible K⁺ participation during the discharge process. Ex situ characterization further confirms reversible surface phase evolution between CoOOH and Co(OH) 2 during charge-discharge cycling, forming a mixed-phase interface that contributes to structural stability and sustained electrochemical performance at high current densities. Supported by density functional theory (DFT) migration barrier calculations, Raman analysis, and suppressed Mo dissolution, the results demonstrate that MXene plays a role in enhancing ion transport kinetics. This study provides mechanistic insight into interface-regulated ion transport in bimetallic nitride/MXene hybrids and highlights their potential for advanced hybrid energy storage systems.
articles.summary_en: Researchers developed an interface-engineered cobalt molybdenum nitride/Ti₃C₂Tₓ MXene hybrid with enhanced ion transport during discharge and improved structural stability. The findings provide mechanistic insight into hybrid energy-storage electrodes but remain at the research stage.

articles.title_original: A dataset of electrosprayed Ti3C2Tx MXene on PAN-derived carbon fibers for enhanced capacitive energy storage
articles.title_en: Dataset Tracks MXene-Coated Carbon Fibers for Capacitive Energy Storage
articles.excerpt_original: This dataset contains the experimental data supporting the article “Electrospray Deposition of Ti3C2Tx MXene onto Carbon Nanofibers: Morphology Control for Enhanced Electrochemical Energy Storage”, submitted to New Carbon Materials. The data were generated at Universidad Carlos III de Madrid (Spain). We produced free-standing carbon fiber mats by electrospinning polyacrylonitrile (PAN), followed by stabilization and carbonization. We then deposited delaminated Ti3C2Tx MXene nanosheets onto the mats by electrospraying, varying the dispersion concentration (0.5–5 mg mL⁻1) and sprayed volume (30–300 µL) to obtain different coating morphologies.We characterized the materials by electron microscopy, X-ray diffraction, and X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy. We evaluated their electrochemical performance by cyclic voltammetry, galvanostatic charge–discharge, electrochemical impedance spectroscopy, and long-term cycling over 10,000 cycles. We processed and plotted the data in OriginPro.The dataset is organized by figure, following the numbering of the main manuscript (Fig. 1–6) and the Supporting Information (Fig. S1–S11). Each figure is provided as an OriginPro project file (.opju) containing the plotted data and graphs, together with an image of the figure. The .opju files can be opened with OriginPro or with the free Origin Viewer (https://www.originlab.com/viewer/). Schematic illustrations and the graphical abstract are not included, as they do not contain experimental data.
articles.summary_en: Researchers at Universidad Carlos III de Madrid compiled experimental data on Ti3C2Tx MXene electrosprayed onto PAN-derived carbon-fiber mats. The dataset examines how coating concentration and sprayed volume affect morphology and electrochemical performance, including cycling over 10,000 cycles.

articles.title_original: Reversible Electric-Field-Induced Changes in the Thermal Resistance of Hexagonal Boron Nitride
articles.title_en: Electric fields reversibly alter thermal resistance in hexagonal boron nitride
articles.excerpt_original: Abstract Understanding the behavior of ultrawide-bandgap (UWBG) materials under high electric fields is essential for advancing next-generation power electronics. While electrical degradation processes have been widely studied, the influence of high electric fields on thermal transport remains largely unexplored. Here, we report the first experimental measurements of changing thermal resistance under an applied electric field in a UWBG material, using single-crystalline hexagonal boron nitride (h-BN) as a model system. We observe substantial, and sometimes reversible, changes in thermal resistance during prolonged exposure to a strong DC electric field. These results reveal a previously unrecognized sensitivity of phonon transport to high-field electrical stressing and show that thermal resistance can serve as a sensitive probe of electric-field-induced material evolution that remains undetected by conventional electrical characterization. More broadly, this work establishes thermal transport measurements as a powerful tool for investigating high-field phenomena in UWBG materials.
articles.summary_en: Researchers report the first experimental measurements of electric-field-induced changes in thermal resistance in single-crystal hexagonal boron nitride. The findings suggest thermal transport can reveal material evolution under high-field stress in ultrawide-bandgap power-electronics materials, including changes not detected electrically.

articles.title_original: High-efficiency removal of malachite green G dye from wastewater aqueous solutions by two-dimensional hexagonal boron nitride: adsorption mechanism by density functional theory
articles.title_en: Hexagonal Boron Nitride Enables High-Efficiency Malachite Green Dye Removal
articles.summary_en: Researchers used density functional theory to investigate how two-dimensional hexagonal boron nitride adsorbs malachite green dye from wastewater. The study provides mechanistic insight relevant to adsorbent design for aqueous pollutant removal.

articles.title_original: Schottky barrier height modulation and memristive behavior in a mechanically exfoliated $MoS_2$ flake with multiple lateral electrodes
articles.title_en: MoS₂ Memristors Show Tunable Schottky Barriers and Resistance Switching
articles.excerpt_original: Van de Waals materials possess great potential as core active materials for novel electronics, optoelectronics, and sensing applications. In particular, transition metal dichalcogenides (TMDs) and other low-dimensional materials, such as hexagonal boron nitride and binary oxides exhibit memristive behavior, making them attractive candidates as building blocks for resistive memories and neuromorphic computing devices. In this work, we investigate two-terminal lateral memristors based on mechanically exfoliated few layer $MoS_2$ flakes. We study the influence of the Schottky barrier height (SBH) as a function of the contact area. We report different SBHs from 60 meV up to 208 meV in the same $MoS_2$ flake and analyze the effect of the SBH in the memristive-like $J-V_{DS}$ curves and the observed non-volatile/volatile resistance switching. Our results highlight the importance of contact engineering to obtain different memristive properties in $MoS_2$-based devices.
articles.summary_en: Researchers studied lateral memristors based on mechanically exfoliated few-layer MoS₂, measuring Schottky barrier heights from 60 to 208 meV within a single flake. The findings link contact engineering to volatile and non-volatile resistance switching, supporting device optimization for resistive memory and neuromorphic electronics.

articles.title_original: Field-tunable Schottky-to-ohmic contact transition and visible-light absorption enhancement in a newly predicted 2D B3S/graphene van der Waals heterostructure
articles.title_en: Predicted B3S/Graphene Heterostructure Enables Field-Tunable Contacts
articles.excerpt_original: Two-dimensional (2D) semiconductors with tunable interfacial and optical properties are vital for advanced nanoelectronic and optoelectronic devices. Using global structure prediction and first-principles calculations, we identify a previously unknown low-energy 2D B3S phase with a distinctive S–B–B–S layered configuration. The B3S monolayer is dynamically and thermally stable (up to 2000 K under ab initio molecular dynamics) and exhibits an indirect wide bandgap of 4.21 eV (HSE06) and strong intrinsic ultraviolet absorption. A B3S/graphene van der Waals heterostructure forms an n-type Schottky contact at equilibrium. Under a perpendicular electric field, the interface shows a reversible Schottky-to-Ohmic transition, achieving field-tunable carrier polarity and barrier control through charge redistribution and built-in electric fields. Moreover, visible-light absorption is significantly enhanced and spectrally tunable owing to interlayer electronic hybridization. These findings introduce a novel 2D B3S semiconductor and demonstrate a feasible strategy for designing field-responsive, broadband optoelectronic heterostructures with reconfigurable transport and photoresponse properties.
articles.summary_en: First-principles calculations predict a stable 2D B3S/graphene van der Waals heterostructure with a reversible Schottky-to-ohmic transition under an electric field. The structure also offers enhanced, tunable visible-light absorption for reconfigurable optoelectronic devices.

articles.title_original: Synergistic SERS Enhancement in Ag NW/WSe2 Heterostructures: Interfacial Charge Transfer and Layer-Dependent Sensitivity
articles.title_en: Ag Nanowire–WSe₂ Heterostructures Enhance Layer-Dependent SERS Signals
articles.excerpt_original: Abstract Surface-enhanced Raman scattering (SERS) substrates based on metal/two-dimensional (2D) semiconductor composites offer unique advantages, yet macroscopic ensemble platforms suffer from spatial nonuniformity that obscures interfacial mechanisms. A deterministic SERS platform was constructed by precisely integrating an individual Ag NW across silica–monolayer (1L) and monolayer–bilayer (2L) WSe2 boundaries. The Ag NW–1L WSe2 hybrid exhibits Raman intensities up to 7.4 times higher than Ag NWs on silica and 4.0–4.5 times higher than Ag NWs on 2L WSe2. Density functional theory calculations reveal that Ag donates ∼0.36 e to WSe2, while 1L WSe2 confines the transferred electrons to its surface, yielding a high surface charge density. In contrast, 2L WSe2 exhibits spatial charge delocalization across the bilayer, reducing the surface electron density. This work offers a controllable strategy to eliminate ensemble averaging and clarifies layer-dependent interfacial dynamics in metal–2D semiconductor heterostructures.
articles.summary_en: Researchers developed a deterministic surface-enhanced Raman scattering platform by integrating individual silver nanowires across monolayer and bilayer WSe₂ boundaries. Monolayer WSe₂ produced up to 7.4-fold stronger Raman signals than silver nanowires on silica, attributed to localized interfacial charge transfer.

articles.title_original: From projected phase to surface-state electrostatics in FIB-prepared semiconductor lamellae
articles.title_en: Model Improves Electrostatic Analysis of FIB-Prepared Semiconductor Lamellae
articles.excerpt_original: Abstract Off-axis electron holography provides quantitative access to projected electrostatic potentials in semiconductor devices. However, focused-ion-beam (FIB) preparation can substantially modify the near-surface electrostatics of transmission electron microscopy lamellae. These effects redistribute the internal potential through surface-state charging, band bending, and screening, making the measured phase difficult to interpret in terms of the crystalline device core. Here, we establish a physical interpretation of the multilayer Simple and Intuitive Model for Potentials (SIMP), a three-dimensional forward-modeling framework for reconstructing electrostatic potentials from projected electron-holographic phase images, by relating its phenomenological parameters to effective screening lengths, near-surface band bending, electric fields, and charge carrier densities. As an illustration, the framework is then applied to symmetrically doped Si p-n junction lamellae prepared at final FIB acceleration voltages of 2 kV and 30 kV. The results show that reduced projected fields can arise primarily from averaging over preparation-modified near-surface regions rather than from intrinsically weak junction electrostatics. This advances multilayer SIMP from an empirical reconstruction method towards a physically anchored framework for quantitative electrostatic characterization of FIB-prepared semiconductor nanostructures.
articles.summary_en: Researchers developed a physically grounded interpretation of the multilayer SIMP framework for reconstructing electrostatic potentials from electron-holography data. Tests on FIB-prepared silicon p–n junction lamellae show that preparation-induced surface effects can make intrinsic junction fields appear weaker.

articles.title_original: Photovoltaic Modulation of MoS2 Transistors via Interfacial Photoelectron Injection in Pn-Si/MoS2/h-BN Heterostructures
articles.title_en: Photovoltaic Gating Enhances MoS₂ Transistor Photoresponse
articles.excerpt_original: Abstract Two-dimensional (2D) semiconductor transistors offer attractive optoelectronic functionality beyond the scaling limits of conventional silicon technology. However, conventional 2D phototransistors often suffer from limited photoresponse performance, high energy consumption, and unstable threshold voltage. To overcome these challenges, we demonstrate a photovoltaic modulated field-effect transistor based on a pn-Si/MoS2/h-BN heterostructure. Under visible illumination, photogenerated electrons accumulate near the pn-Si/MoS2 interface and are vertically injected into the adjacent MoS2 conduction channel. A current change from approximately 3.8 μA to 11.2 μA is observed when illumination is switched on during a gate-voltage sweep, corresponding to a switching-event current ratio of approximately 2.95. Concurrently, the device exhibits reversible current modulation during the recorded optical ON/OFF cycles. Wavelength-dependent measurements further elucidate a critical competition between injection-driven carrier enhancement and high-field suppression effects. First-principles calculations using monolayer MoS2/h-BN heterostructure models further show that electron doping increases the electrical conductivity of MoS2 by increasing the occupation of conduction-band states and improving carrier transport. These results demonstrate optical modulation in Si-supported MoS2 devices and motivate further investigation of the contributions from interfacial carrier transfer and photovoltaic gating.
articles.summary_en: Researchers demonstrated a photovoltaic-modulated MoS₂ transistor using a pn-Si/MoS₂/h-BN heterostructure, achieving an approximately 2.95-fold switching-event current increase under visible illumination. The study attributes modulation to interfacial photoelectron injection and supports the mechanism with first-principles calculations.

articles.title_original: Quantum spin Hall insulating phase in Nb–Ta double-layer honeycomb (DLHC) lattice
articles.title_en: Nb–Ta 2D lattices predicted as quantum spin Hall insulators
articles.excerpt_original: The recent experimental synthesis of AlSb in a double-layer honeycomb (DLHC) structure has sparked interest in studying a new type of two-dimensional (2D) material. This successful synthesis confirms the previous theoretical prediction that traditional semiconductors are stable in the DLHC structure within the ultrathin limit. In this study, we investigated six Nb–Ta-based compounds and considered their 2D wurtzite, 2D zinc blende, AA configuration, and DLHC structural configurations using first-principles calculations. Among these configurations, the DLHC structure is the most energetically favorable for all the investigated compounds. The phonon dispersions show that NbP, NbAs, TaP, and TaAs compounds have no significant negative frequencies, confirming their dynamic stability. Using the HSE06 hybrid functional approach, NbP, NbAs, TaP, and TaAs are found to host nontrivial phases (Z2 = 1) upon inclusion of spin–orbit coupling (SOC), with positive system bandgap ranging from 110 to 250 meV. For the representative compound NbAs, the nontrivial topology is rigorously established by an independent irreducible representation analysis using the Fu–Kane parity criterion, which reveals an SOC-driven band inversion at the Γ point and yields Z2 = 1 in full agreement with the Wannier charge center method. The presence of gapless edge states with explicit connectivity between time-reversal invariant momentum points, finite spin Berry curvature, and spin Hall conductivity further verifies the nontrivial topological nature of these compounds. Our results indicate that the Nb–Ta-based DLHC materials have potential applications in both topological and electronic devices.
articles.summary_en: First-principles calculations identify dynamically stable NbP, NbAs, TaP, and TaAs double-layer honeycomb structures with nontrivial topological phases and bandgaps of 110–250 meV. The findings indicate potential use in topological and electronic devices, but remain theoretical.

articles.title_original: Graphene-family nanomaterials as pharmacological agents: mechanisms, therapeutic index and translational barriers
articles.title_en: Graphene-family nanomaterials face major pharmacological and safety barriers
articles.excerpt_original: Graphene-family nanomaterials, including graphene oxide, reduced graphene oxide and graphene quantum dots, are under investigation as drug carriers and as materials with their own biological activity. Their pharmacological behaviour depends on the specific formulation. Lateral size, layer number, oxidation, defects, aggregation and surface coating govern protein adsorption, membrane contact, cellular uptake, redox and inflammatory signalling, organ distribution and clearance. The same features that raise drug loading or photothermal conversion can injure membranes, mitochondria and lysosomes and prolong retention in the liver, spleen or lung. Increases in anticancer activity in cell and animal studies often reflect a change in drug exposure rather than a direct action of the carrier, and many experiments omit unloaded-carrier and free-drug controls. Quantitative pharmacokinetics, repeated-dose toxicology and comparisons with established nanocarriers remain limited. No graphene formulation is an approved systemic medicine. This review connects defined material properties with molecular mechanisms and in vivo disposition, separates carrier effects from drug effects, and states the quality, pharmacological and safety evidence required before clinical development.
articles.summary_en: A Wiley review finds that graphene oxide, reduced graphene oxide and graphene quantum dots have potential as drug carriers and bioactive materials, but their effects vary substantially with formulation and physicochemical properties. Limited pharmacokinetic, repeated-dose toxicology and comparative evidence—and the absence of an approved systemic formulation—continue to impede clinical translation.

articles.title_original: Oxidation controlled nonlinear optical absorption in 2D materials derived from MXene
articles.title_en: Controlled oxidation tunes nonlinear optical absorption in MXene-derived materials
articles.excerpt_original: As a rapidly expanding family of 2D materials, MXenes have attracted considerable interest for photonic applications, and their oxide derivatives offer an additional degree of freedom for tailoring their optical responses. Here, we systematically investigate how controlled oxidation regulates the nonlinear optical absorption (NOA) of Ti3C2Tx MXene. The MXene films are prepared using a transfer-free, layer-by-layer self-assembly method, followed by conversion into MXene oxide (MXO) and TiO2 through a two-step oxidation process. The NOA behaviors of the MXene and corresponding MXO and TiO2 derivatives are characterized by Z-scan measurements at ~515, ~800, and ~1030 nm, showing distinct wavelength-dependent responses. All three materials exhibit reverse saturable absorption (RSA) at ~800 nm, and progressive oxidation induces saturable absorption (SA)-to-RSA transitions at ~515 and ~1030 nm. This transition is particularly notable at ~1030 nm, where the nonlinear absorption coefficient β changes from ~−9.05 × 10−10 m/W for MXene to ~2.07 × 10−9 m/W for TiO2. Intensity-dependent measurements further reveal distinct variations in β among the three materials. These results establish controlled oxidation as an effective strategy for engineering the NOA of MXene-derived materials and provide insight into the evolution of their nonlinear optical properties, offering a versatile material platform for potential nonlinear optical applications such as optical modulation and optical limiting.
articles.summary_en: Researchers systematically show that oxidizing Ti₃C₂Tₓ MXene into MXene oxide and TiO₂ changes its nonlinear optical absorption across multiple wavelengths. The findings support potential optical modulation and optical-limiting applications, but no company involvement is reported.

articles.title_original: Renewable Sandwich Roll-Like Electrode Based on Hollow Ni-NiCx Microsphere and MXene for Constructing a Portable Non-Enzymatic Glucose Sensor
articles.title_en: Renewable MXene–Nickel Electrode Enables Portable Non-Enzymatic Glucose Sensing
articles.excerpt_original: Abstract A renewable electrode without relying on traditional supporting electrodes is expected to reduce the use-cost and improve the testing efficiency. Herein, a novel renewable electrode that is hollow Ni-NiCx microspheres@carbonized rice-paper@few-layer Ti3C2Tx nanosheets (Ni-NiCx@CRP@Ti3C2Tx) is prepared through the processes of drop-casting, curling, pyrolysis, and molding. Such a Ni-NiCx@CRP@Ti3C2Tx electrode with sandwich roll-like structure can be directly utilized as the working electrode for non-enzymatic glucose sensing. The main performance parameters include 0.5–280.0 μM of linear detection range, 79 nM of detection limit, and 2860 μA mM−1 cm−2 of sensitivity. The high-performance behaviors of Ni-NiCx@CRP@Ti3C2Tx electrode are attributed to the optimized interlayer relationships of the sandwich roll-like structure. First, the Ni-NiCx layer provides high-efficiency active sites for the electrochemical oxidation of glucose. Second, the Ti3C2Tx layer provides an excellent conductive network for the collection of electrochemical signals. More importantly, the rapidly renewable strategy of Ni-NiCx@CRP@Ti3C2Tx electrode is proposed through the self-designed electrode shear for 1st−10th cutting. Ultimately, a prototype of portable electrochemical sensor composed of the renewable Ni-NiCx@CRP@Ti3C2Tx electrode, the adjustable working electrode system and the self-designed electronic system is established for detecting glucose in urine sample. Our work presents a novel approach for developing renewable electrodes for electrochemical sensing.
articles.summary_en: Researchers developed a cuttable, renewable electrode combining hollow Ni–NiCx microspheres, carbonized rice paper, and Ti3C2Tx MXene nanosheets. The prototype detected glucose in urine with a 79 nM detection limit and a 0.5–280 μM linear range.

articles.title_original: Three-dimensional thermally conductive structural materials enabled by dual-network design in aramid/boron nitride papers
articles.title_en: Dual-network aramid/boron nitride honeycomb improves structural heat spreading
articles.excerpt_original: Efforts to enhance thermal conductivity have largely been confined to functional composites and films, while the need for efficient heat propagation in mechanically loaded structures remains less explored. Here, we fabricate a thermally conductive honeycomb by constructing a dual-network architecture within aramid paper, where post-impregnated boron nitride nanosheets form interconnected thermal pathways while the fibrous scaffold maintains mechanical integrity. The composite paper reaches ∼6.82 W m−1 K−1 in-plane conductivity, ∼70 MPa tensile strength, and dielectric loss as low as ∼0.0062. In honeycomb form, it delivers ∼64% higher thermal conductivity and ∼95% faster heat spreading than pristine aramid honeycomb, offering a practical structural solution for thermal management.
articles.summary_en: Researchers developed a thermally conductive honeycomb by integrating boron nitride nanosheets into aramid paper while retaining mechanical strength. The composite achieved approximately 6.82 W m⁻¹ K⁻¹ in-plane conductivity and delivered 95% faster heat spreading than pristine aramid honeycomb, indicating potential for load-bearing thermal-management structures.

articles.title_original: Multicomponent Isotope Engineering of Phonon Polaritons in Hexagonal Boron Nitride
articles.title_en: Isotope Engineering Tunes Low-Loss Phonon Polaritons in Hexagonal Boron Nitride
articles.excerpt_original: Isotopic enrichment provides a non-invasive means of tuning the vibrational and optical properties of van der Waals crystals (vdW) without altering their lattice structure. We investigate two doubly enriched hexagonal boron nitride (hBN) compositions, h10B15N and h11B15N, to determine how isotope substitution on both sublattices modifies mid-infrared hyperbolic phonon polaritons (HPhPs). Polarization-resolved room temperature and cryogenic far-field reflectance measurements reveal optical-phonon blue shifts of approximately 35 cm-1 in h10B15N relative h11B15N, translating both Reststrahlen bands (RBs) and their polariton dispersions. For the upper RB, the combined accessible range expands from 1360-1614 cm-1 in natural hBN to 1356-1640 cm-1 across the B- enriched 14N crystals and 1339-1640 cm-1 when the 15N enriched crystals are included. Near-field imaging confirms deeply sub-diffractional propagation and shows that both crystals exhibit lower polariton damping and longer lifetimes than natural hBN, with performance comparable to monoisotopically enriched crystals. Further, we compare the conventional reduced-mass description with a phenomenological two-component inverse-mass model that captures the isotope dependence of the phonon frequencies and LO-TO coupling while resolving the contributions of the individual sublattices. These results establish multicomponent isotope engineering as a materials design strategy for positioning the HPhPs spectral range while preserving low-loss propagation in polar vdW crystals.
articles.summary_en: Researchers show that enriching both boron and nitrogen isotopes in hexagonal boron nitride shifts mid-infrared hyperbolic phonon-polariton bands by up to approximately 35 cm⁻¹. The engineered crystals retain low damping and long polariton lifetimes, establishing multicomponent isotope engineering as a route to tunable, low-loss van der Waals photonics.

articles.title_original: Assessing the effect of polariton interactions on the formation of polariton condensates in 2D Molybdenum Diselenide (MoSe2)
articles.title_en: Polariton interactions hinder condensate formation in 2D MoSe2
articles.excerpt_original: Two Dimensional (2D) transition metal dichalcogenide (TMD) materials are defined by the emergence of new properties resulting from collective quantum effects and by holding promise for their quantum applications. Recently, through adiabatic impulse approximation (AIA) and the Brundobler-Elser (BE) conjecture, we investigated coherent control of polaritonic entities in 2D TMD materials of 2H types [Physica Scripta 97(2), 025801 (2022)] , which induces several applications. We realized that, among 2D TMD materials of 2H types, 2D Molybdenum Diselenide (MoSe 2 ) is the best candidate to form polariton condensates. In the present research work, we reported the influence of polariton-polariton interactions on the formation of polariton condensates in 2D TMD MoSe 2 embedded in 2D microcavity. Under rotating wave and adiabatic impulse approximations, we investigated both Landau Energy Levels (LELs) and Landau-Zener (LZ) diabatic and adiabatic transition probabilities of the system of laser cooled and trapped polariton in 2D TMD MoSe 2 embedded in 2D microcavity. Numerical results reveal that polariton-polariton interactions reduce the total energy of the system and governs the transition probability of finding the cooled and trapped polariton in the ground state. Thus, by providing a means to manipulate the dynamics of polaritons under intense laser radiation, polariton-polariton interactions are detrimental to the formation of polariton condensates. We formally recommended the utilization of laser cooled and trapped polaritons in 2D TMD MoSe 2 embedded in 2D microcavity with intense laser radiation and under the influence of low polariton-polariton interactions for successful implementation of quantum devices.
articles.summary_en: A study models polariton–polariton interactions in MoSe2 embedded in a microcavity and finds they reduce system energy while adversely affecting ground-state condensation. The authors recommend low interaction strengths and laser-cooled, trapped polaritons for quantum-device implementation.

articles.title_original: Graphene-Based Multifunctional Protective Clothing - A Technical Review
articles.title_en: Review assesses graphene-based multifunctional protective clothing
articles.excerpt_original: Graphene and its derivatives have been of great interest for multifunctional protective clothing due to their mechanical properties, electrical conductivity, thermal properties, and ability to improve the performance of textiles. The applications of graphene-based materials as a protective textile are reviewed, focusing on the flame resistance, chemical protection, ballistic and stab resistance, electromagnetic interference (EMI) shielding, and thermal regulation domains. It also examines the fabrication methods such as dip coating, spray coating, electrophoretic deposition, fibre spinning, printing, and laser-induced graphene, in terms of processing properties, scalability, and difficulties in integration with the textile material. Apart from performance and manufacturing aspects, the review includes prominent hurdles to real-life application such as production costs, durability of the coating, wash resistance, and possible environmental and toxicological effects. The possibility of release of graphene-related particles during laundering and abrasion, as well as degradation of materials, means that it is important to consider material retention and potential for exposure to the environment throughout the protective garment's service life. The life cycle of graphene-based textile composites, including their environmental fate, long-term toxicity, recycling, and end-of-life, however, has not been sufficiently established and needs further investigation. In summary, the properties of graphene-based fabrics, combined with their lightweight and flexible nature, as well as their multi-functional nature, provide promising prospects for the development of protective materials with multiple functions. To advance their responsible development and commercialisation for defence, h
articles.summary_en: The review examines graphene-enabled protective textiles for flame, chemical, ballistic, stab, EMI-shielding, and thermal-regulation applications, alongside scalable fabrication methods. It identifies cost, durability, wash resistance, particle release, toxicity, recycling, and end-of-life management as barriers to commercialization.

articles.title_original: Topological phase singularity engineering in a graphene–Fabry–Pérot hybrid system
articles.title_en: Graphene–Fabry–Pérot Hybrid Enables Topological Phase Sensing
articles.excerpt_original: Conventional optical phase control relies on propagation-induced phase accumulation, which becomes challenging at the atomic scale because of the extremely limited optical path length. Here, topological phase singularities are realized in a monolayer graphene-Fabry-Pérot hybrid system by coupling the dispersive optical response of graphene with Fabry-Pérot interference in a SiO2/Si substrate. The resulting complex reflection zeros can be interpreted as critical-coupling states of an open non-Hermitian optical system and are accompanied by 2π phase winding with nonzero topological charges. The steep phase response near the singularities enables refractive-index sensing with a maximum phase-sensitivity magnitude of 2450.8 degrees/RIU. Structural perturbations primarily shift the singularity positions while preserving their phase-winding characteristics. Furthermore, cascaded Fabry-Pérot cavities extend the system into a multi-singularity regime, enabling the controllable generation, transport, and pairwise annihilation of oppositely charged singularities under continuous parameter tuning. These results establish an atomically thin platform for topological phase engineering and phase-enhanced optical sensing.
articles.summary_en: Researchers engineered topological phase singularities in a monolayer graphene–Fabry–Pérot system, achieving phase sensitivity up to 2450.8 degrees per refractive-index unit. Cascaded cavities enabled controllable generation and manipulation of multiple singularities, indicating potential for advanced optical sensing and phase engineering.

articles.title_original: Flexible and oxidation-resistant graphene@SiC nanofiber fabrics
articles.title_en: Graphene–SiC Nanofiber Fabrics Deliver High-Temperature EMI Shielding
articles.excerpt_original: Carbon-based macroscopic architectures hold immense potential in flexible electronics owing to their low density and exceptional electrical conductivity. However, their susceptibility to oxidative degradation at elevated temperatures severely restricts their deployment in extreme environments. Here, we report the design of flexible graphene@silicon carbide core-shell nanofiber fabrics (G@SiC NFFs) fabricated via coaxial electrospinning and sequential thermal processing. The resulting hierarchical structure features a highly conductive graphene nanofiber core coaxially shielded by an oxidation-resistant SiC shell, seamlessly integrated via a robust heterointerface. Benefiting from their unique architecture, 20 wt% polycarbosilane-derived G@SiC NFFs achieved a frequency-averaged X-band electromagnetic interference (EMI) shielding effectiveness exceeding 80 dB at thicknesses of approximately 85-95 μm. A representative sample with a thickness of approximately 80 μm exhibited a shielding effectiveness of 85.5 dB and retained 76.7 dB after oxidation in air at 650 °C for 1 h. Remarkably, the fabrics exhibit robust electrothermal stability during prolonged exposure to an alcohol-lamp flame at 650 °C and thermal shock using an alcohol-torch flame at 1,100 °C, while also enabling reliable Joule heating up to 650 °C under ambient conditions. This work presents a strategy for developing lightweight and thermally resilient carbon-based electronics, paving the way for high-temperature EMI shielding and related extreme-environment applications.
articles.summary_en: Researchers developed flexible graphene@silicon carbide core-shell nanofiber fabrics that achieved over 80 dB X-band EMI shielding at roughly 85–95 μm thickness. The fabrics retained 76.7 dB shielding after oxidation at 650 °C and supported Joule heating to 650 °C, indicating potential for extreme-environment electronics and dual-use shielding.

articles.title_original: Tuning correlated states in rhombohedral pentalayer graphene with magnetic encapsulation
articles.title_en: Magnetic encapsulation tunes correlated states in pentalayer graphene
articles.excerpt_original: Rhombohedral graphene multilayers provide a flexible platform for correlated physics associated with their flat-band electronic structure. While a variety of correlated states appear in these systems as a function of bias and electrostatic doping, promoting specific correlated flavor symmetry breaking states remains a challenge. Here we show that magnetic encapsulation by CrGeTe3 achieves this in rhombohedral pentalayer graphene, by using switchable exchange couplings induced by ferromagnetic substrates. We show that correlations in rhombohedral multilayers at charge neutrality strongly renormalize the exchange proximity splitting,giving rise to collective spin modes whose character is switched by the parallel or antiparallel alignment of the encapsulation. We further show that upon doping of the flat bands, spin triplet f-wave superconducting solutions emerge, whose layer and spin selectivity is controlled by the magnetic encapsulation, hosting in-gap excitations at the edges. Our results establish magnetic alignment as a means to control spin symmetry breaking and unconventional superconductivity in rhombohedral pentalayer graphene.
articles.summary_en: Researchers show that CrGeTe3 magnetic encapsulation can control spin-symmetry breaking and exchange interactions in rhombohedral pentalayer graphene. The approach produces switchable collective spin modes and predicts layer- and spin-selective triplet f-wave superconductivity under doping.

articles.title_original: Out-of-plane interference effects in angle-resolved photoemission of epitaxial graphene
articles.title_en: ARPES study reveals interference effects in epitaxial graphene
articles.excerpt_original: The epitaxial growth of monolayer graphene by Si sublimation of 6H-SiC(0001) is one of the most effective ways of producing large-scale monocrystalline graphene samples of high quality. However, graphene is left interacting with a reconstructed carbon buffer layer known as zerolayer graphene (ZLG) and the SiC substrate underneath. Beyond the mere creation of Dirac cone replicas, the effect of this interaction on photoemission measurements is poorly understood. We utilized synchrotron radiation for photon-energy-dependent angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy (ARPES) to investigate the complex final-state interactions of photoelectrons within the heterostructure of monolayer graphene, ZLG, and SiC. We identify multiple resonances in the photoemission intensity of the Dirac cone as a function of photon energy that originate from interlayer interference, confirmed with a multiple scattering model. We also demonstrate for the first time that the relative intensity of the replica bands induced by the $(6\sqrt{3} \times 6\sqrt{3})\text{R}30^\circ$ reconstruction scales with the electron kinetic energy. Finally, we resolved four nondispersing electronic states, which originate from the ZLG. Our findings show that the three-dimensional (3D) structure of SiC and ZLG manifests itself in the photoemission from two-dimensional (2D) epitaxial graphene. By revealing how 3D substrate architecture dictates the photoemission of a 2D layer, this work establishes a crucial framework for investigating the electronic structure of complex heterostructures via ARPES.
articles.summary_en: Researchers used synchrotron ARPES and multiple-scattering modeling to identify photon-energy-dependent interlayer interference in monolayer graphene on SiC. The study also resolved electronic states from the zerolayer graphene buffer, clarifying how the three-dimensional substrate influences graphene’s measured electronic structure.

articles.title_original: Nitramine-based energetic composites of graphene oxide with improved properties
articles.title_en: Graphene Oxide Enhances Nitramine Energetic Composites
articles.excerpt_original: Nanographene-based energetic materials continue to attract attention as a new class of functional energetic composites. Graphene-derived nanomaterials can act simultaneously as desensitizing additives, heat-transfer promoters, structural reinforcements, and catalysts for thermal decomposition and combustion. In particular, graphene oxide (GO), owing to its high specific surface area, two-dimensional morphology, abundant oxygen-containing functional groups, and tunable interfacial chemistry, is a promising platform for the design of nitramine-based energetic composites. This review summarizes recent progress in composites of GO and cyclic nitramine explosives, including RDX, HMX, and CL-20. Emphasis is placed on fabrication methods, including solution blending, electrostatic self-assembly, surface coating, and in situ assembly, which enable intimate contact between energetic crystals and GO sheets. The effects of GO incorporation on thermal stability, impact and friction sensitivity, mechanical properties, ignition behavior, decomposition kinetics, and combustion performance are critically evaluated. GO can provide a physical barrier and energy dissipation network around energetic crystals, reducing the formation of hot spots and thereby improving resistance to external mechanical stimuli. At the same time, its high thermal conductivity and functionalized surface may alter heat and mass transport, promote interfacial reactions, and modify the multistep thermal decomposition of nitramines. Functionalized derivatives, including reduced, doped, metal-decorated, and nitrated graphene oxides, offer further opportunities to balance desensitization with enhanced reactivity and energy release. Overall, GO-based composites represent promising candidates for the development of saf
articles.summary_en: A review examines graphene oxide composites with RDX, HMX, and CL-20, focusing on fabrication methods and effects on sensitivity, thermal decomposition, ignition, and combustion. Graphene oxide may improve safety through energy dissipation while also modifying heat and mass transport and interfacial reactivity.

articles.title_original: Robust Ambient‐Pressure‐Dried MXene Aerogels via Multiscale Structural Engineering
articles.title_en: Robust MXene aerogels retain structure after ambient-pressure drying
articles.excerpt_original: ABSTRACT Ambient pressure drying is a promising route to scale up MXene aerogels, but it is limited by severe capillary collapse during solvent evaporation. Here, robust ambient‐pressure‐dried MXene aerogels are fabricated via multiscale structural engineering. At the molecular scale, ethanol acts as both a low‐surface‐tension solvent and a poor solvent inducing MXene phase separation, revealing its role in stabilizing wet gels beyond reducing surface tension. This process increases the contact between oxygen‐containing groups on MXene and hydroxyl groups of TEMPO‐oxidized cellulose nanofiber (TOCNF), leading to a dense hydrogen‐bonding network. More importantly, the phase separation degree serves as a microstructural descriptor linking ethanol‐induced structural evolution to mechanical reinforcement, providing a basis for optimizing capillary‐resistant aerogels. Macroscopically, polydopamine‐modified loofah acts as a reinforcing framework to form a reinforced concrete‐like architecture with the MXene/TOCNF matrix. The molecular hydrogen bonding network and the macroscopic skeleton jointly preserve an intact porous structure after drying. The resulting aerogel exhibits a Young's modulus of 0.57 MPa, an electromagnetic shielding effectiveness of 74.6 dB, excellent infrared stealth performance, and a rapid Joule heating response. This work clarifies the hidden role of ethanol in ambient pressure drying and establishes a microstructure‐guided design principle for robust multifunctional MXene aerogels.
articles.summary_en: Researchers developed MXene/TOCNF aerogels reinforced with polydopamine-modified loofah, using ethanol-induced phase separation and multiscale hydrogen bonding to prevent capillary collapse during drying. The aerogels achieved 74.6 dB electromagnetic shielding, infrared stealth, rapid Joule heating, and a Young’s modulus of 0.57 MPa, indicating potential in defense and thermal-management applications.

articles.title_original: Oxygen-Driven Etching of MAX Phases Assisted by HF Vapor (OxyVap-HF) for MXenes Synthesis
articles.title_en: Oxygen-Assisted HF Vapor Route Enables Greener MXene Synthesis
articles.excerpt_original: MXenes are conventionally produced by immersing MAX phases in fluoride-containing acids, where removal of A elements proceeds via their proton-driven oxidation leading to H 2 gas evolution accompanied by fluoride complexation with A n+ . Here we introduce a different, oxygen-driven HF vapor assisted route (OxyVap-HF) in which a precursor MAX phase, such as Ti 3 AlC 2 , is held separated from a dilute HF solution reservoir and etched by oxygen available in air, assisted by HF/H 2 O vapor helping to maintain access of oxygen to A element layers. Importantly, in OxyVap-HF the MAX phase is never in direct contact with liquid, therefore the same dilute HF solution can be used multiple times without purification or any other treatment, minimizing safety risks and environmental burden of MXene synthesis, thereby directly addressing the need for greener MXene synthesis methods. Mechanistically, in the oxygen-containing atmosphere of the OxyVap-HF the etching reaction consumes O 2 rather than evolving H 2 . Gas volume analysis, scavenging of O 2 with pyrogallol, experiments in controlled Ar/O 2 /air atmospheres, and Raman spectroscopy of the gas phase demonstrate a switch from traditional proton-driven, H 2 -evolving etching under Ar, to oxygen-driven etching in air. The HF/H 2 O ratio controls MAX phase conversion, assisting with the removal of Al–O-containing intermediates formed during etching, installing terminations, and expanding the interlayer spacing, thus yielding MXenes that can be further delaminated. We show that an aqueous HF solution with concentration as low as 3 wt% can be used repeatedly in OxyVap-HF process, consistently yielding new batches of delaminable MXenes.
articles.summary_en: Researchers introduce OxyVap-HF, a liquid-free etching method that uses oxygen and HF/H₂O vapor to convert MAX phases into delaminable MXenes. The process repeatedly uses dilute 3 wt% HF, potentially reducing hydrogen evolution, chemical waste, and safety risks.

articles.title_original: 3D dual-support MXene/graphene oxide composite with in-situ grown nanoflowers toward high-stability and high-sensitivity glucose biosensing
articles.title_en: MXene/Graphene Oxide Composite Enables Sensitive Glucose Biosensing
articles.summary_en: Researchers report a three-dimensional dual-support MXene/graphene oxide composite incorporating in-situ-grown nanoflowers for glucose biosensing. The study targets improved sensor stability and sensitivity.

articles.title_original: Double-quantum-enhanced coherent control and magnetic sensing of spin defects in hexagonal boron nitride
articles.title_en: Double-Quantum Control Improves hBN Spin-Defect Magnetometry
articles.excerpt_original: The negatively charged boron vacancy ($V_{\mathrm{B}}^{-}$) in hexagonal boron nitride (hBN) is a promising spin defect for quantum sensing in two-dimensional material systems. Previous hBN experiments have mainly exploited the two spin-triplet ground-state single-quantum transitions separately. Here we implement a double-quantum driving scheme based on simultaneous resonant microwave excitation of both ground-state single-quantum transitions, establishing coherent control of the $Δm_s=2$ manifold in a $V_{\mathrm{B}}^{-}$ ensemble. We compare the resulting double-quantum response with the corresponding single-quantum protocol under identical experimental conditions. The double-quantum protocol enhances the optical readout contrast and yields a 2.6-fold signal-to-noise improvement in AC magnetometry. We further use the double-quantum relaxation channel as a differential probe of electric-field and strain noise, showing that the present data are compatible with correlated-surface or volume-distributed fluctuations, while short-range uncorrelated surface-noise models are disfavored within the assumptions of our analysis. These results establish double-quantum coherent control and frequency-resolved AC magnetometry in hBN spin ensembles, and identify the sample-dependent measurements needed to determine the microscopic origin of the dominant relaxation channels.
articles.summary_en: Researchers demonstrated double-quantum coherent control of boron-vacancy spin defects in hexagonal boron nitride, achieving a 2.6-fold signal-to-noise improvement in AC magnetometry. The work also uses relaxation measurements to probe electric-field and strain noise in hBN.

articles.title_original: Examining the Effect of Hexagonal Boron Nitride on Morphological and Chemical Properties of Biopolymers Using Dual-Beam Methodology
articles.title_en: hBN Improves Silver Nanowire Distribution in Biopolymer Nanocomposites
articles.excerpt_original: Biocompatible and biodegradable polymers have attracted increasing interest for biomedical applications such as drug delivery systems, implants, and medical devices. In this study, nanocomposites based on widely used biodegradable synthetic biopolymers, polylactic acid (PLA) and polycaprolactone (PCL), were investigated to enhance their structural performance. The solvent-dependent effect of hexagonal boron nitride (hBN) addition on the chemical and morphological distribution of silver nanowires (AgNWs) within PCL and PLA matrices was systematically examined. High-resolution morphological characterization was performed using focused ion beam–scanning electron microscopy (FIB-SEM), enabling simultaneous cross-sectioning and imaging. Inner morphology was analyzed by SEM, while elemental distributions were evaluated using energy-dispersive spectroscopy (EDS). The results indicated that hBN incorporation contributed to an improved distribution of AgNWs in both polymer matrices. This effect appeared to be more pronounced in PLA-based nanocomposites prepared using chloroform, where AgNWs showed a comparatively more uniform spatial distribution than in the acetone-prepared samples. In addition, PLA- and PCL-based AgNWs/hBN nanocomposites prepared in chloroform exhibited enhanced mechanical strength and thermal stability during gallium ion milling. Overall, the findings highlight the critical role of solvent selection and hBN incorporation in optimizing the structural properties and performance of biopolymer-based nanocomposites for biomedical applications.
articles.summary_en: Researchers found that hexagonal boron nitride improved silver nanowire distribution in PLA and PCL matrices, with the strongest effect observed in chloroform-prepared PLA composites. The resulting nanocomposites also showed enhanced mechanical strength and thermal stability during gallium ion milling, supporting potential biomedical applications.

articles.title_original: Damped polarizability and first hyperpolarizability of large systems with hybrid functionals: self-consistent and Lanczos solvers
articles.title_en: Lanczos Method Enables Optical-Response Calculations for Large hBN Flakes
articles.excerpt_original: We present a damped coupled-perturbed Kohn-Sham method to compute the dynamical polarizability and first hyperpolarizability of finite systems, implemented in the CRYSTAL code for semi-local, global and range-separated hybrid functionals. The approach is based on the adiabatic time-dependent density functional theory for the complex-valued (hyper)polarizabilities, describing optical phenomena such as absorption, and the nonlinear second-harmonic generation, rectification and Pockels effect. These are obtained either at individual frequencies with a self-consistent solver based on Pulay extrapolation, or at an arbitrary grid of frequency and damping factors with a Lanczos solver, from which the first-order amplitudes required in the hyperpolarizability can be reconstructed. With hybrid functionals, the self-consistent solver tends to become impractical at some point beyond the absorption onset, where there are many excitations for which the external frequency lies between their energy and those of their contributing single-particle transitions, and its convergence eventually stalls for large systems. In contrast, the convergence of the Lanczos method is essentially independent of size, hence the cost of the dynamical response calculation scales with system size as the hybrid ground-state calculation. The implementation is validated in a small molecule and, as an application, we study the first and second-order optical response of a series of hexagonal boron nitride flakes of up to 324 atoms. The use of range-separated hybrid functionals allows to capture the strongly-bound first excitation of the monolayer, and evidences the failure of the self-consistent method to converge excitations with strong electron-hole attraction.
articles.summary_en: Researchers developed and validated a hybrid-functional computational method for calculating dynamical polarizability and first hyperpolarizability in large systems. Applied to hexagonal boron nitride flakes of up to 324 atoms, the Lanczos solver addressed convergence limitations affecting self-consistent calculations of strongly bound excitations.

articles.title_original: Quantum Embedding from Molecular to Crystalline Environments at the Cost of a Gas-Phase Calculation
articles.title_en: Embedded DFT Enables Lower-Cost Quantum Modeling of Molecular and Crystalline Systems
articles.excerpt_original: We present a direct-space formulation and implementation of quantum density functional theory (DFT) embedding for molecular active subsystems embedded in frozen environments (hosts) of arbitrary dimensionality, from finite molecular hosts to extended systems. The host is computed once without the embedded molecule (the guest) and is represented only by its electron density fitted in an atom-centered auxiliary Gaussian basis together with its nuclear charges with the periodic electrostatics separated into an explicit near-field and a continuous fast-multipole far-field operator. The method allows the removal of host atoms from this representation to create vacancies or other voids without requiring a supercell creation. Analytic nuclear gradients are also implemented, enabling structural relaxation of the active subsystem. We demonstrate the versatility of the approach through applications to adsorbates on periodic surfaces and molecules embedded in bulk solvent environments. For CO on MgO(001), we show that DFT-in-DFT converges rapidly and reproduces the periodic interaction energy within 0.44 kJ/mol while reducing the cost by a factor of 27. Real-time time-dependent embedded DFT (RT-TDDFET) of methylenecyclopropene in periodic water is showcased to produce a ~0.6 eV solvatochromic blue shift, while strong-field propagation of CO2 on hexagonal boron nitride (hBN) yields substrate-induced effects at the cost of a gas-phase propagation. Coupling the embedding scheme to excited-state correlated wave function theory methods such as CC2 yields a solvent shift within 0.01 eV of supermolecular CC2 references, while reducing the computational cost by over 500 times.
articles.summary_en: Researchers present a quantum-embedding method that models molecular subsystems within environments ranging from finite molecules to periodic crystals, while supporting structural relaxation and excited-state calculations. Demonstrations report up to 27-fold cost reduction for CO on MgO and over 500-fold reduction when coupled with CC2 calculations, including applications involving water and hexagonal boron nitride.

articles.title_original: Hybrid 2D g-C 3 N 4 /SrFe 12 O 19 magnetically recoverable photocatalyst: synergistic heterojunction for enhanced photodegradation of pharmaceuticals in an aqueous medium
articles.title_en: Magnetically Recoverable Photocatalyst Degrades Pharmaceuticals in Water
articles.excerpt_original: Active pharmaceutical contaminants (APCs), i.e. antibiotics, cause significant environmental and health risks. A magnetically recoverable 2D g-C 3 N 4 /SrFe 12 O 19 heterojunction enables efficient photocatalytic degradation of tetracycline as a model APC.
articles.summary_en: Researchers developed a 2D graphitic carbon nitride/strontium ferrite heterojunction that photocatalytically degrades tetracycline in aqueous media. Its magnetic recoverability could support catalyst reuse in pharmaceutical-contaminant treatment, although the excerpt provides no performance or scalability data.

articles.title_original: Pd Single‐Atom Engineered Janus BiOCl/MXene Heterostructure for Printed Self‐Decoupled Temperature‐Humidity Dual‐Mode Sensors
articles.title_en: Pd Single-Atom BiOCl/MXene Sensor Enables Self-Decoupled Temperature–Humidity Monitoring
articles.excerpt_original: ABSTRACT The advancement of flexible sensing technologies is of paramount importance in biomedical engineering. However, achieving high‐fidelity multi‐modal temperature‐humidity sensing without inter‐channel cross‐talk and computational post‐processing remains a formidable challenge due to overlapping transduction mechanisms. In this study, an unprecedented electron‐ion synergistic functional material, featuring a unique inherent self‐decoupling capability, was developed based on the Janus hierarchical heterostructure. Through interfacial chemical engineering of Pd single‐atom anchoring and heterogeneous‐nucleation‐driven vertical growth of BiOCl on hollow MXene, the constructed material architecture successfully establishes fundamentally segregated electronic and ionic stimulus‐response pathways. Specifically, humidity fluctuations trigger ultra‐fast quasi‐2D proton conduction facilitated by localized potential wells and electronic redistribution generated around atomically dispersed Pd sites, while temperature gradients induce entropy‐driven carrier diffusion within the conductive MXene network. By suppressing signal cross‐talk through rigorous mechanistic orthogonality, the fabricated sensing array exhibits outstanding response characteristics (37.5/50 ms for humidity response/recovery and 25/62.5 ms for high/low‐temperature response), alongside superior oxidation resistance and robust functional durability (enduring 5000 cycles of testing). Ultimately, leveraging this multi‐modal sensing platform and machine learning algorithm, the integrated closed‐loop therapeutic system enables accurate evaluation of wound healing progression as well as on‐demand drug release, pioneering a new paradigm for next‐generation flexible electronics and adaptive healthcare modalities.
articles.summary_en: Researchers developed a printed Janus BiOCl/MXene heterostructure with palladium single atoms that separates ionic humidity responses from electronic temperature responses, reducing cross-talk. The sensor supports rapid dual-mode detection and was integrated into a machine-learning wound-healing and drug-release system.

articles.title_original: Flexible and Attachable Terahertz Polarizer Enabled by Laser-induced Graphene
articles.title_en: Laser-Induced Graphene Enables Flexible, Transferable Terahertz Polarizer
articles.excerpt_original: Abstract Terahertz (THz) polarizers are indispensable for polarization-sensitive spectroscopy, imaging, and communication systems. Conventional metal-based wire-grid polarizers, despite their high performance, rely on complex photolithography and thin-film deposition processes that incur substantial costs and constrain scalability. Here, we demonstrate a flexible and attachable THz polarizer enabled by laser-induced graphene (LIG)—a three-dimensional porous carbon material synthesized in a single step via direct laser writing on polyimide. The polarizer consists of 2 layers of LIG wire-grid geometry with a period of 60 µm and a strip width of 50 µm, and is fabricated through a streamlined, mask-free protocol and subsequently peeled from its rigid substrate for transfer onto arbitrary flexible supports. Experimental results show that the polarizer yields an extinction ratio less than − 25 dB across 0.25–1.0 THz, and this value keeps no more than − 20 dB under bending radii down to 22.5 mm. These results establish LIG as a compelling material platform for low-cost, scalable, and transferable THz polarizers, bridging the gap between high-performance metal-based devices and practical manufacturing requirements.
articles.summary_en: Researchers demonstrated a mask-free, two-layer laser-induced graphene wire-grid polarizer fabricated on polyimide and transferred to flexible supports. It achieved an extinction ratio below −25 dB across 0.25–1.0 THz and maintained better than −20 dB when bent to a 22.5 mm radius, indicating scalable potential for THz imaging, spectroscopy, and communications.

articles.title_original: Hierarchically Porous PDMS/ZIF-8@h-BN Bilayer Composite Membrane Enabling Synergistic Passive Daytime Radiative Cooling and Efficient Thermal Conduction for Electronic Thermal Management
articles.title_en: PDMS/h-BN Bilayer Membrane Enables Passive Cooling and Heat Spreading
articles.excerpt_original: The advancement of 5G and emerging 6G communications drives the integration and miniaturization of outdoor electronics, triggering an exponential surge in chip heat flux and severe challenges for low-energy passive thermal management. Passive daytime radiative cooling (PDRC) has emerged as a novel zero-energy cooling technology. Herein, a bilayer PDRC composite (B-PDRC) integrating radiative cooling and in-plane thermal conduction is designed and fabricated. The top radiative cooling layer is a hierarchically porous Polydimethylsiloxane (PDMS)/zeolitic imidazolate framework-8 (ZIF-8) foam prepared via a template-sacrificial method combined with vacuum impregnation, while the bottom thermally conductive layer is a PDMS/hexagonal boron nitride (h-BN) dense film fabricated by solution casting. The multiscale scattering induced by micron-sized pores and 600-800 nm ZIF-8 nanoparticles delivers a high solar reflectance of 94.45%, and the C-N bonds of ZIF-8 boost the average atmospheric window emissivity to 93.22%, compensating for the emissivity valley of neat PDMS. The h-BN fillers construct continuous thermal conduction paths, elevating the in-plane thermal conductivity to 0.92 W m-1 K-1 at 20 wt % of h-BN, a 179% enhancement compared to neat PDMS. Indoor tests demonstrate a maximum temperature drop of 11.9 °C for a charging smartphone covered with B-PDRC. Outdoor measurements under sunny conditions achieve a maximum subambient cooling of 8.8 °C, and a 14.8 °C temperature reduction for an operating smartphone. Furthermore, B-PDRC exhibits excellent hydrophobic self-cleaning performance (water contact angle of 135.4°), flexibility, mechanical robustness, long-term durability under UV and humid conditions, and universal adhesion to various substrates. articles.summary_en: Researchers developed a porous PDMS/ZIF-8 radiative-cooling layer paired with a PDMS/h-BN thermally conductive film for electronic thermal management. The membrane reduced operating smartphone temperatures by up to 14.8 °C outdoors while increasing in-plane thermal conductivity by 179% versus neat PDMS.

articles.title_original: Thermal effect on the anomaly-induced electromechanical response in gapped graphene
articles.title_en: Thermal Effects on Electromechanical Responses in Gapped Graphene
articles.excerpt_original: Mechanical deformation of gapped graphene can act on Dirac quasiparticles as an emergent gauge field. When this deformation field couples to the same current as the electromagnetic field, the parity anomaly produces a mixed electromechanical Chern-Simons response: a phonon electric field drives a transverse electrical current, and a phonon magnetic field binds charge. Previous zero-temperature results predict a sharp change in the response when the chemical potential crosses the band edge. We show that finite temperature replaces this sharp feature by a universal smooth crossover controlled only by the ratios of temperature, gap, and chemical potential. The response remains almost quantized in the insulating regime, is rounded over a gate window of order temperature near the band edge, and approaches the doped Berry-curvature result with a controlled Sommerfeld correction. We apply the result to two experimentally useful drives: a traveling flexural wave, which produces a transverse second-harmonic current, and a dynamic phonon mixed with a static ripple, which produces a fundamental-frequency signal. The same gate-temperature line shape controls both signals. This gives a direct way to separate the anomaly-induced current from ordinary electromechanical backgrounds and to extract the effective gap and electronic temperature in graphene devices.
articles.summary_en: Researchers show that finite temperature smooths the sharp electromechanical response predicted when graphene’s chemical potential crosses the band edge, with the crossover governed by temperature, gap, and chemical potential. The model predicts measurable transverse current signals from flexural waves and dynamic phonons, potentially enabling separation of anomaly-induced effects and extraction of graphene device parameters.
